Here are the real trees of both lab pages, captured by the tests with Playwright's ariaSnapshot(). Compare them line by line:

BrokenFixed 
- banner:
  - link "FreshCart":
    - /url: "#"
  - button
  - text: "0"
- main:
  - heading "Fresh fruit" [level=1]
  - heading "Today's picks" [level=4]
  - search:
    - searchbox "Search products"
    - button "Go"
  - article:
    - img
    - paragraph: Shimla Apple, 1 kg
    - paragraph: Delivered in 10 minutes
    - text: ADD
  - button "Delivery info"

- banner:
  - link "FreshCart":
    - /url: "#"
  - button "Cart"
  - status: 0 in cart
- main:
  - heading "Fresh fruit" [level=1]
  - heading "Today's picks" [level=2]
  - search:
    - text: Search products
    - searchbox "Search products"
    - button "Go"
  - article:
    - paragraph: Shimla Apple, 1 kg
    - paragraph: Delivered in 10 minutes
    - button "Add Shimla Apple to cart": ADD
  - button "Delivery info"
In the broken tree Means - button with no name A screen reader says just "button". Which one? (A3) - text: "0" A number with no meaning, and nothing is announced when it changes (A9) heading … [level=4] right after level 1 The outline skips levels 2 and 3 (A8) - img with no name An image the user is told exists but not what it is (A10) - text: ADD Not a button at all: it has no role, so it can't be found in a list of buttons or activated (A5) searchbox "Search products" It has a name, taken from the placeholder. That's why axe passed it, but the placeholder vanishes as soon as you type (A4)

docs.title: Step 4: A screen reader (15 minutes)
docs.text:
Use the one built into your system, or the free NVDA on Windows:

Screen reader Start / stop Next item Headings list Activate VoiceOver (macOS) Cmd+F5 Ctrl+Option+Right Ctrl+Option+U (rotor), then arrows Ctrl+Option+Space NVDA (Windows, free) Ctrl+Alt+N / Ins+Q Down Ins+F7 (elements list); H jumps to the next heading Enter Narrator (Windows) Ctrl+Win+Enter Caps Lock+Right turn on scan mode (Caps Lock+Space), then H Caps Lock+Enter TalkBack (Android) / VoiceOver (iOS) Settings → Accessibility Swipe right Rotor / reading controls Double-tap

Then do three things on the lab:

  1. Listen to the whole page from the top. Does every image, button and field make sense out of context?
  2. Open the headings list. Is it a sensible outline of the page?
  3. Do the main task: add the apple to the cart. Did you hear that it worked?

On the broken page you'll hear roughly "button" for the cart (which button?), nothing at all when the count changes (A9: the only problem that just a screen reader shows), and you can't add the apple without the mouse.

Screen readers differ

Each screen reader and browser pair speaks a little differently. Test with at least one desktop and one mobile reader: VoiceOver + Safari, and NVDA + Chrome or Firefox, cover most users.

docs.title: Step 5: Zoom, reflow and emulation (5 minutes)
docs.text:
• Zoom to 200 % (Ctrl++ / Cmd++): text grows, nothing overlaps or gets cut off.
  • 320 px wide in the device toolbar: no sideways scrolling (WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow).
  • Rendering → Emulate vision deficiencies: is anything shown by colour alone (red = error, green = OK)?
  • Rendering → prefers-reduced-motion: reduce: animations calm down.

docs.title: The 10 problems
docs.text:
Try to find each one with the steps above before opening the answer. All the fixes come from a11y-lab-fixed.html, which is generated from the broken page by scripts/gen_bug_lab.py, so the code here is exactly what was tested.

A1. The page has no language · WCAG 3.1.1 · found by axe

Without lang, a screen reader guesses which voice and pronunciation to use, and often guesses wrong.

<html>

<html lang="en">
A2. Grey text is too faint · WCAG 1.4.3 · found by axe and the DevTools colour picker

#b0b0b0 on white is 2.2 : 1; normal text needs 4.5 : 1.

.eta {
  margin: 0;
  color: #b0b0b0;                           /* A2 */
  font-size: 0.85rem;
}

color: #5b6370;                           /* FIX A2: 6.1 : 1 on white (was 2.2 : 1) */
A3. The cart button has no name · WCAG 4.1.2 · found by axe and the accessibility tree

An icon-only button with aria-hidden on its SVG has no text at all, so it's announced as just "button".

<button class="icon-btn" type="button">
  <svg width="22" height="22" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M7 18a2 2 0 1 0 0 4 2 2 0 0 0 0-4Zm10 0a2 2 0 1 0 0 4 2 2 0 0 0 0-4ZM5.2 4H2V2h4.8l.9 2H22l-3.4 8H8.5l-.9 2H19v2H5l2.4-4.6L5.2 4Z"/></svg>
</button>

<button class="icon-btn" type="button" aria-label="Cart">
  <svg width="22" height="22" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M7 18a2 2 0 1 0 0 4 2 2 0 0 0 0-4Zm10 0a2 2 0 1 0 0 4 2 2 0 0 0 0-4ZM5.2 4H2V2h4.8l.9 2H22l-3.4 8H8.5l-.9 2H19v2H5l2.4-4.6L5.2 4Z"/></svg>
</button>

aria-label gives it a name. Keep aria-hidden="true" on the icon so it isn't read as well.

A4. The search box is labelled only by its placeholder · WCAG 3.3.2 · missed by axe, found by the tree + common sense

The browser uses the placeholder as the accessible name, so axe passes it. But the placeholder disappears as soon as you type, it's usually low-contrast, and some assistive tech ignores it. Use a real <label>, here visually hidden because the design has no room, and keep the placeholder for an example:

<form class="search" role="search">
  <input type="search" name="q" placeholder="Search products">
  <button type="submit">Go</button>
</form>

<label class="visually-hidden" for="q">Search products</label>
<input id="q" type="search" name="q" placeholder="e.g. apples, milk">

.visually-hidden {                        /* hidden on screen, still read by screen readers */
  position: absolute;
  width: 1px;
  height: 1px;
  overflow: hidden;
  clip-path: inset(50%);
  white-space: nowrap;
}
A5. ADD is a div · WCAG 2.1.1, 4.1.2 · missed by axe, found by the keyboard and the tree

A <div> with onclick can't get focus, doesn't react to Enter or Space, and has no button role. Nothing in the code is technically invalid, so automated tools can't tell it was meant to be a button.

<div class="add" onclick="addToCart()">ADD</div>

<button class="add" type="button" onclick="addToCart()" aria-label="Add Shimla Apple to cart">ADD</button>

A real <button> gets focus, keyboard activation and the role for free. The aria-label makes "ADD" specific when there are many products on the page ("Add Shimla Apple to cart"), and it still contains the visible word ADD, so voice-control users can say "click ADD".

A6. The focus ring was removed · WCAG 2.4.7 · missed by axe, found by the keyboard

outline: none on :focus makes keyboard users lose their place completely.

a:focus, button:focus, input:focus {
  outline: none;                            /* A6 */
}

:focus-visible {                          /* FIX A6: a clear ring for keyboard users only */
  outline: 3px solid #2563eb;
  outline-offset: 2px;
}

:focus-visible shows the ring for keyboard focus but not on mouse clicks, which is usually why people removed it in the first place. The blue #2563eb has 5.2 : 1 contrast against white.

A7. The info box isn't a real dialog · WCAG 2.1.1, 2.4.3 · missed by axe, found by the keyboard

Opening it leaves focus on the button behind it, Esc does nothing, and the × is a <span> that can't be reached at all.

<button class="info-btn" type="button" onclick="openInfo()">Delivery info</button>
<div class="dialog" id="info" hidden>
  <p>We deliver from 6 am to midnight, every day, in about 10 minutes.</p>
  <span class="close" onclick="closeInfo()">×</span>
</div>

function openInfo() {
  document.querySelector("#info").hidden = false;
}
function closeInfo() {
  document.querySelector("#info").hidden = true;
}

Use the native <dialog> with showModal(). It moves focus inside, keeps Tab inside, closes on Esc, makes the page behind inert, and returns focus to the button when it closes:

<dialog class="dialog" id="info" aria-labelledby="info-title">
  <h2 id="info-title">Delivery info</h2>
  <p>We deliver from 6 am to midnight, every day, in about 10 minutes.</p>
  <form method="dialog">
    <button class="close" aria-label="Close">×</button>
  </form>
</dialog>

function openInfo() {
  document.querySelector("#info").showModal();   // moves focus in, traps Tab, Esc closes, focus returns after
}

.dialog {
  max-width: 360px;
  border: 0;
  padding: 16px 40px 16px 16px;
  border-radius: 12px;
  background: #fff;
  box-shadow: 0 8px 32px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.3);
}
.dialog::backdrop { background: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.4); }
.dialog h2 { margin: 0 0 8px; font-size: 1.1rem; }
.close { position: absolute; top: 8px; right: 8px; width: 32px; height: 32px; border: 0; border-radius: 50%; background: none; font: inherit; font-size: 1.4rem; cursor: pointer; }
A8. Headings jump from level 1 to level 4 · WCAG 1.3.1 · found by axe and the tree

Screen-reader users navigate by headings; a jump from h1 to h4 suggests missing sections. Choose the level by structure and set the size with CSS.

<h1>Fresh fruit</h1>
<h4>Today's picks</h4>

<h2>Today's picks</h2>
A9. The cart count changes silently · WCAG 4.1.3 · found only by a screen reader

Sighted users see the number change. Screen-reader users hear nothing, because focus didn't move and the number isn't in a live region.

<span class="count" id="count">0</span>

<span class="count" role="status"><span id="count">0</span><span class="visually-hidden"> in cart</span></span>

role="status" makes it a polite live region: when its text changes, screen readers announce it ("1 in cart") without moving focus. The visually hidden " in cart" gives the bare number a meaning.

A10. The image has no alt attribute · WCAG 1.1.1 · found by axe and the tree

With no alt at all, some screen readers read the file name ("apple dot svg").

<img src="apple.svg" width="96" height="96">

<img src="apple.svg" width="96" height="96" alt="">

Here the product name is written right next to the picture, so the image adds nothing and alt="" marks it as decorative (otherwise the name is heard twice). If the image carried information the text doesn't, such as a photo on a product detail page, describe it: alt="Six red Shimla apples in a paper bag".

docs.title: All fixed
docs.text:
a11y-lab-fixed.html: 0 rules failed

The fixed page is also checked with the keyboard and the dialog in a real browser on every change:

18-a11y-lab: 4 checks, 0 failures
  ✔ axe: the broken page fails 5 rules; the fixed page passes all of them
  ✔ keyboard (broken): Tab skips ADD and focus is invisible; (fixed): ADD is a Tab stop with a 3px focus ring
  ✔ dialog (broken): focus stays behind it, Esc does nothing, × can't be reached; (fixed): modal, focus moves in, Esc closes and returns focus
  ✔ accessibility tree: what assistive tech gets from each page (saved for the docs)

docs.title: Who found what
docs.text:
# Problem WCAG axe Keyboard Tree Screen reader A1 No page language 3.1.1 ✓ ✓ A2 Low contrast 1.4.3 ✓ A3 Unnamed icon button 4.1.2 ✓ ✓ ✓ A4 Placeholder as the only label 3.3.2 ✗ ✓ ✓ A5 <div> as a button 2.1.1, 4.1.2 ✗ ✓ ✓ ✓ A6 Focus ring removed 2.4.7 ✗ ✓ A7 Fake dialog 2.1.1, 2.4.3 ✗ ✓ ✓ A8 Skipped heading levels 1.3.1 ✓ ✓ ✓ A9 Silent cart count 4.1.3 ✗ ✓ A10 Image without alt 1.1.1 ✓ ✓ ✓

No single method finds everything. Together they take about 30 minutes per page, and much less once they're a habit.

docs.title: A checklist for every pull request
docs.text:
• axe / Lighthouse accessibility: no violations (ideally automated in CI)
  • Tab through every new control: reachable, visible focus, works with Enter / Space, Esc closes overlays
  • Every new image has the right alt (descriptive or "")
  • Every new field has a <label>; errors are in text and linked with aria-describedby
  • Icon-only buttons have an aria-label
  • Dynamic updates that matter (cart, errors, results count) are in a live region
  • Headings still form a sensible outline
  • 200 % zoom and 320 px width still work
  • For a new widget (tabs, menu, combobox): tried with a screen reader once

docs.title: Bug Lab: Find the 7 Bugs
docs.text:
Beginner Intermediate

This little FreshCart page has 7 bugs planted in it. Each one is the kind you'll meet every week, and each is best found with a different DevTools tool. Find them with DevTools, not by reading the source: the point is to practise the tools from Debugging with DevTools.

Open the Bug Lab in a new tab and press F12 there. DevTools works best on a page of its own rather than inside this frame.

Run it from a web server, not by double-clicking

If you download the file and open it from disk (file://…), Chrome blocks fetch() completely and the Console says Fetch API cannot load file:///…/offer.json. URL scheme "file" is not supported. That hides bug 6. Serve the folder instead: VS Code's Live Server, or python3 -m http.server in the folder, then open http://localhost:8000/bug-lab.html.

Each bug below has its symptom, the tool to reach for, and steps. Try it yourself, then open the answer. The fixes come from bug-lab-fixed.html, which is generated from the broken page by scripts/gen_bug_lab.py, so every fix shown here is exactly what runs there.

docs.title: Bug 1: the page scrolls sideways on a phone
docs.text:
• Symptom: at phone width you can drag the whole page left and right, and there's a white strip on the right.

  • Tool: device toolbar + Elements (+ a Console snippet).

  • Press Ctrl+Shift+M (Cmd+Shift+M) and set the width to 375.

  • Paste the find-overflow snippet into the Console. It prints the culprit; hover the result to highlight it on the page.
  • Select it in Elements and look at Computed → width.
Answer

The promo banner has a fixed width: 420px, which is wider than a 375 px phone (343 px of room after padding):

.promo {
  width: 420px;                     /* BUG 1 */
  margin: 0 0 16px;
  padding: 12px 16px;
  border-radius: 12px;
  background: #2563eb;
  color: #fff;
}

Fix: let it be at most 420 px:

max-width: 420px;                 /* FIX 1: may be up to 420px, but never wider than its container */

Fixed widths are the most common cause of sideways scrolling. Prefer max-width, %, or min(420px, 100%).

docs.title: Bug 2: the price is grey, not green
docs.text:
• Symptom: the CSS clearly says .price { color: #0c831f; }, but the prices are grey.

  • Tool: Elements → Styles.

  • Right-click a price → Inspect.

  • In Styles, find color: #0c831f under .price. Is it struck through?
  • Look above it for the rule that won, and hover both selectors to compare their specificity.
Answer

.card p has specificity (0,1,1) (one class + one element) and beats .price at (0,1,0) (one class), even though .price comes later in the file. Order only decides between equal specificities.

.card p {
  margin: 4px 0 12px;
  color: #555;
}
.price {
  color: #0c831f;                   /* BUG 2: why is the price grey? */
  font-weight: 700;
}

Fix: make the price rule more specific, (0,2,0):

.card .price {                      /* FIX 2: (0,2,0) now beats .card p (0,1,1) */
  color: #0c831f;
  font-weight: 700;
}

Don't reach for !important: it wins this fight but starts an arms race you'll lose later. See Cascade, Specificity & Box Model.

docs.title: Bug 3: the cards are in one column on a wide screen
docs.text:
• Symptom: on a desktop, the three product cards are stacked in one tall column instead of sitting side by side.

  • Tool: Elements → grid badge + Styles.

  • Inspect the <div class="grid">. It has a grid badge: click it to draw the overlay. How many columns?

  • Look at its rules in Styles. One declaration has a warning icon.
Answer

A typo in the property name: grid-template-column (no s). Browsers silently ignore a property they don't know, so the grid falls back to one automatic column. DevTools shows it struck through with a warning icon ("Unknown property name").

.grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-column: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(200px, 1fr));   /* BUG 3 */
  gap: 16px;
}

grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(200px, 1fr));  /* FIX 3: columns, with an s */

docs.title: Bug 4: all the badges pile up in the corner of the page
docs.text:
• Symptom: "20% OFF", "NEW" and "FRESH" should sit on each card's picture. Instead they're stacked on top of each other near the top-left of the page.

  • Tool: Elements → Computed (on the badge and its ancestors).

  • Inspect a badge. Computed → position is absolute, with top: 8px; left: 8px. 8 px from what?

  • Select its parent .card. What is its position?
Answer

An absolutely positioned element is placed relative to its nearest positioned ancestor (one whose position isn't static). No card is positioned, so all three badges are placed relative to the page itself, at the same spot.

.card {
  padding: 12px;
  border: 1px solid #e3e6ea;
  border-radius: 12px;
  background: #fff;
}
.badge {
  position: absolute;               /* BUG 4 */
  top: 8px;
  left: 8px;
  padding: 2px 8px;
  border-radius: 4px;
  background: #2563eb;
  color: #fff;
  font-size: 0.7rem;
  font-weight: 700;
}

Fix: make each card the reference box:

position: relative;               /* FIX 4: the badges are now positioned inside their card */

docs.title: Bug 5: clicking ADD shows an error
docs.text:
• Symptom: click ADD. The cart badge stays at 0, and the Console turns red.

  • Tool: Console → Sources.

  • Open the Console. The error (captured from a real run in Chrome) reads:

    Uncaught TypeError: Cannot set properties of null (setting 'textContent')
    at HTMLDivElement.<anonymous> (bug-lab.html:125:53)

  • Click bug-lab.html:125 to jump to the line. Something on that line is null.

  • In the Console, run the selector from that line on its own: document.querySelector(".cart-count"). Then inspect the badge in Elements and compare its real class.
Answer

querySelector returns null when nothing matches, and you can't set textContent on null. The HTML uses class="cart-badge", but the script looks for .cart-count.

document.querySelector(".grid").addEventListener("click", (event) => {
  const button = event.target.closest(".add");
  if (!button) return;
  const card = button.closest(".card");

  total = total + card.dataset.price;                           // BUG 7
  document.querySelector("#total").textContent = total;

  count++;
  document.querySelector(".cart-count").textContent = count;    // BUG 5
});

document.querySelector(".cart-badge").textContent = count;    // FIX 5: the class in the HTML is cart-badge

"Cannot read/set properties of null" almost always means a selector found nothing. Copy the selector into the Console to check it.

docs.title: Bug 6: “Couldn't load today's offer”
docs.text:
• Symptom: the yellow strip says Couldn't load today's offer (HTTP 404) instead of the offer.

  • Tool: Network.

  • Open Network, filter to Fetch/XHR, and reload.

  • Find the red row. What URL did the page ask for? What's the status?
  • Compare it with the files that actually exist next to the page.
Answer

The page requests offer.json, but the file is called offers.json. The server answers 404 Not Found. The code handles that properly (it checks response.ok and shows a message), which is why there's no crash, only a wrong message.

async function loadOffer() {
  const offer = document.querySelector("#offer");
  try {
    const response = await fetch("offer.json");                  // BUG 6
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`);
    const data = await response.json();
    offer.textContent = `🔥 ${data.title}`;
  } catch (err) {
    offer.textContent = `Couldn't load today's offer (${err.message})`;
  }
}
loadOffer();

const response = await fetch("offers.json");                 // FIX 6: the file is offers.json

docs.title: Bug 7: the total says ₹0189
docs.text:
• Symptom: after one ADD on the apple (₹189), the total reads ₹0189. Add the banana and it becomes ₹018949. No error at all.

  • Tool: Sources → breakpoint + Watch.

  • In Sources, open bug-lab.html and put a breakpoint on the total = total + … line.

  • Click ADD. When it pauses, hover card.dataset.price. Are there quotes around the value?
  • Add typeof card.dataset.price to the Watch pane.
Answer

card.dataset.price is the string "189": data attributes are always strings. 0 + "189" joins text instead of adding, giving "0189". No error is thrown, so only stepping through and looking at the values shows the problem.

total = total + Number(card.dataset.price);                   // FIX 7: data-* values are strings

This is the same trap as "3" + 1 in JavaScript lesson 1. Better still for money: store whole paise (data-price="18900") as FreshCart does.

docs.title: All fixed
docs.text:
Both pages are checked in a real browser on every change. The checks prove each bug really happens in the broken page and is gone in the fixed one, and run the console snippets from the guide against them:

17-devtools-bug-lab: 6 checks, 0 failures
  ✔ bugs 1 and 3: the broken page scrolls sideways on a phone and its grid is one column; fixed: no scroll, 3 columns
  ✔ bugs 2 and 4: the price is grey and the badges pile up at the top of the page; fixed: green price, badges inside cards
  ✔ bugs 5 and 7: ADD throws a TypeError and the total reads ₹0189; fixed: no error, ₹189 then ₹238, badge counts
  ✔ bug 6: the offer request is a 404; fixed: 200 and the offer shows
  ✔ console snippets: find-overflow names the promo banner (and nothing once fixed); outline-all toggles
  ✔ console snippet: log-focus reports each Tab stop in order

docs.title: What each bug taught
docs.text: # Bug Tool that found it Lesson 1 Sideways scroll Device toolbar + snippet Fixed widths break small screens: use max-width 2 Grey price Styles (struck-through rule) Specificity beats source order 3 One column grid badge + Styles warning Typos in CSS fail silently 4 Badges in the corner Computed position absolute needs a positioned ancestor 5 TypeError Console → Sources null = your selector found nothing 6 Offer missing Network Check the status and URL of every request 7 ₹0189 Breakpoint + Watch Data from the DOM is text: convert with Number()

docs.title: Build an E-commerce Page: Start Here
docs.text:
Beginner Intermediate

In this tab you build FreshCart, a responsive grocery store page (think BigBasket, Blinkit or Instacart), one small component at a time. Every line of code is explained. By the end you have a real page that works on a phone and on a desktop, with a working cart.

Open it full-size: store.html. Press Ctrl+Shift+M in DevTools to view it as a phone, click ADD on a few products, then open the cart.

docs.title: How to start (10 minutes of setup)
docs.text:
You need only a browser and a text editor. No Node, no framework, no build step.

  1. Install an editor. VS Code is free. Add the Live Server extension: it reloads the page every time you save.

  2. Create this folder structure. One CSS file per component keeps every file short and easy to find.

    freshcart/
├── store.html          ← the page (all the HTML)
├── css/
│   ├── base.css        ← colours, spacing, reset, buttons   (lesson 1)
│   ├── header.css      ← announcement bar, header, nav     (lesson 2)
│   ├── home.css        ← hero, offers, category tiles      (lesson 3)
│   ├── product.css     ← product card + product grid       (lesson 4)
│   ├── listing.css     ← filters, sort bar, page layout    (lesson 5)
│   ├── cart.css        ← cart drawer                       (lesson 6)
│   └── footer.css      ← footer + mobile bottom nav        (lesson 7)
└── js/
    └── store.js        ← cart, filters and sort            (lessons 4–6)

  3. Type, don't paste. Typing each line is slower but you'll remember it. Paste only when you're stuck.

  4. Right-click → Open with Live Server on store.html. Keep DevTools open (F12) while you work.
  5. After each lesson, resize the browser from wide to narrow and check nothing overflows sideways.

Want the finished files?

Every file in this tab lives in the repository under docs/ecommerce/demos/. Download the folder and open store.html in a browser. Nothing to install.

docs.title: Step 1 before any code: break the page into boxes
docs.text:
Professional frontend developers never start by typing. They look at the design and draw boxes inside boxes. Each box becomes an HTML element; repeated boxes become a component (the same HTML + CSS reused). Here is FreshCart broken into its components:

① Announcement bar ② Logo ③ Location ④ Search box ⑤ Login · Cart (badge) ⑥ Category nav: All · Fruits · Vegetables · Dairy · … (scrolls sideways on a phone) ⑦ Hero banner: headline + button + picture ⑧ Offer ⑧ Offer ⑧ Offer ⑨⑨⑨⑨⑨⑨ ⑩ Filters sidebar ⑪ Toolbar: "Showing 8 products" · Sort by ⑫ Product card⑫⑫⑫ ⑬ Footer: about · links · newsletter ⑭ Cart drawer slides in from the right · ⑮ Bottom nav phones only

Each number is one small component. Notice three things:

  • Components repeat. ⑫ Product card is written once and used eight times. ⑨ Category tile is used six times.
  • Components nest. The header ⑤ contains the cart button, which contains a red count badge.
  • Each component needs one layout tool. A row of things → Flexbox. A 2-D arrangement or a grid of equal cards → Grid.
flowchart TD P["store.html"] --> A["① Announcement"] P --> H["Header"] H --> L["② Logo"] H --> LO["③ Location"] H --> S["④ Search"] H --> AC["⑤ Actions: Login + Cart button + badge"] P --> N["⑥ Category nav"] P --> M["main"] M --> HE["⑦ Hero + ⑧ Offers"] M --> C["⑨ Category tiles × 6"] M --> LI["Listing"] LI --> F["⑩ Filters"] LI --> T["⑪ Toolbar"] LI --> G["Product grid"] G --> PC["⑫ Product card × 8"] P --> D["⑭ Cart drawer"] P --> FO["⑬ Footer"] P --> B["⑮ Bottom nav"]

docs.title: Step 2: decide how it changes on a phone
docs.text:
Write the phone layout first (one column, everything stacked), then add @media (width >= 768px) rules that spread things out on wider screens. This is called mobile first: phones get the simplest CSS, and big screens add to it.

Component Phone (< 768 px) Desktop (≥ 768 px) Tool Header logo · location · cart on row 1, search on row 2 everything in one row Grid grid-template-areas Category nav one row that scrolls sideways one row, fits Flexbox + overflow-x: auto Hero text only text left, picture right Grid columns Offers swipeable carousel three equal boxes Grid + scroll-snap Category tiles 3 per row as many as fit Grid auto-fill Filters collapsed "Filters ▸" button always-open sidebar (≥ 900 px) <details> + Grid Product grid 2 per row as many as fit Grid auto-fill + minmax() Footer stacked 4 columns Grid auto-fit Bottom nav fixed at the bottom hidden position: fixed

docs.title: The lessons
docs.text: # Lesson You learn 1 Page skeleton & design tokens Every line of the HTML boilerplate, a CSS reset, CSS variables, a .container, buttons 2 Header & category nav Sticky header, grid-template-areas, a search form, a cart badge, a sideways-scrolling nav 3 Hero, offers & category tiles clamp() font sizes, gradients, a scroll-snap carousel, an auto-fill grid 4 Product card & product grid The most important e-commerce component: badge, price, ADD button, quantity stepper 5 Listing: filters & sort Sidebar layout, <details>, <fieldset>, filtering and sorting with JavaScript 6 Cart drawer <dialog>, ::backdrop, cart state, money in paise, event delegation 7 Footer & mobile bottom nav Footer grid, newsletter form, position: fixed, :has(), safe areas 8 Put it all together The assembled page, a testing checklist, and exercises to keep practising

docs.title: How each lesson is laid out
docs.text:
1. What you see: the component, live, in a frame you can resize.
  2. HTML, then a line-by-line table explaining every line.
  3. CSS, then a line-by-line table.
  4. Try it exercises, each with a collapsed solution to open after you've had a go, and common mistakes. The code solutions all run together in store-solved.html.

All code on these pages is pulled straight from the files in demos/, so what you read is exactly what runs in the frames. The <!-- --8<-- [start:…] --> comments you'll see in those files are only markers that tell this site which piece to show. You don't need them in your own copy.

Why emoji instead of product photos?

So the demo has no image files to download. In a real store each product picture is an <img>; lesson 4 shows exactly how to write it (width, height, alt, loading="lazy").

docs.title: 1. Page Skeleton & Design Tokens
docs.text:
Beginner

Before any component, every page needs two things: a correct HTML skeleton and a base stylesheet (design tokens, a reset, and a few shared helpers). Get these right once and every later component becomes shorter.

docs.title: The HTML skeleton
Line by line
docs.text: Line Code What it does 1 <!doctype html> Tells the browser "this is modern HTML". Without it the browser switches to quirks mode and copies 1990s bugs, so layouts break in strange ways. 2 <html lang="en"> The root element. lang tells screen readers which voice and pronunciation to use, and helps Google and the browser's translate button. 3 <head> Information about the page. Nothing in <head> is drawn on screen. 4 <meta charset="utf-8"> Text encoding. UTF-8 handles every language and symbol, including ₹ and emoji. Keep it first in <head>. 5 <meta name="viewport" …> The most important line for mobile. Without it a phone pretends to be a 980 px-wide desktop and shrinks everything. width=device-width makes 1 CSS pixel match the phone's width; initial-scale=1 means no zoom. 6 <title>…</title> The text in the browser tab, in bookmarks, and as the blue link in Google results. 7 <meta name="description" …> The grey text under your link in search results. About 150 characters. 8 <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/base.css"> Loads the CSS file. The path is relative to the HTML file: "the css folder next to me". 9 </head> End of the invisible part. 10 <body> Everything visible goes here. 11 <header> A landmark: the top of the site (logo, search, cart). Screen-reader users can jump straight to it. Lesson 2 fills it in. 12 <main id="main"> The unique content of this page. Use exactly one per page. The id lets a "Skip to content" link jump here. 13 <div class="container"> A plain box with no meaning, used only for layout: it limits the width and centres the content. 14 <h1> The page's main heading. One per page; then h2 for sections, h3 inside those. Never skip levels just to get a smaller font. 15 <p> A paragraph. 16 <a class="btn" href="#"> A link styled as a button. Use <a> when it goes somewhere, <button> when it does something on this page. 17 class="btn btn--outline" Two classes: the base button plus a modifier that changes only its colours (BEM naming: block--modifier). 18–20 </div></main><footer> Close the boxes. <footer> is the bottom landmark (lesson 7). 21–22 </body></html> Close the document.

docs.title: Design tokens: name your decisions
docs.text:
A design token is a named value: a colour, a spacing step, a radius. You define it once with a CSS custom property (--name: value) and use it everywhere with var(--name). To change the brand colour of the whole site, you edit one line.

css/base.css (tokens)
:root {
  /* Colours */
  --brand: #0c831f;
  --brand-dark: #0a6b19;
  --brand-soft: #e8f5ea;
  --accent: #f8cb46;
  --danger: #d6342c;
  --text: #1f2329;
  --muted: #5b6370;
  --line: #e3e6ea;
  --surface: #ffffff;
  --page: #f6f7f8;

  /* Spacing scale: use these instead of random pixel values */
  --space-1: 4px;
  --space-2: 8px;
  --space-3: 12px;
  --space-4: 16px;
  --space-6: 24px;
  --space-8: 32px;

  /* Shape and depth */
  --radius: 12px;
  --radius-sm: 8px;
  --shadow: 0 2px 8px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.08);

  /* Page width */
  --container: 1200px;
}
Code What it does :root { … } :root is the <html> element. Variables declared here are visible to every element on the page. --brand: #0c831f; The main green. Buttons, logo and links use it. --brand-dark is the hover colour, --brand-soft a pale tint for backgrounds. --accent, --danger Yellow for highlights and focus rings; red for the cart badge and errors. --text, --muted Main text colour (near-black, softer than pure #000) and grey for secondary text. --line, --surface, --page Border grey, card white, and the light grey page background that makes white cards stand out. --space-1 … --space-8 A spacing scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32 px). Using only these values is what makes a layout look tidy. --radius, --radius-sm Corner rounding: 12 px for cards, 8 px for buttons and inputs. --shadow A soft shadow for hover. rgb(0 0 0 / 0.08) is black at 8 % opacity. --container: 1200px The maximum width of the content on big screens.

docs.title: A small reset
docs.text:
Browsers add their own default styles, and they differ slightly. A reset removes the annoying ones.

css/base.css (reset)
*,
*::before,
*::after {
  box-sizing: border-box;
}

body {
  margin: 0;
  font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;
  font-size: 16px;
  line-height: 1.5;
  color: var(--text);
  background: var(--page);
}

img {
  display: block;
  max-width: 100%;
}

button,
input,
select {
  font: inherit;
}

a {
  color: inherit;
}

[hidden] {
  display: none !important;
}
Code What it does *, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; } Makes width include padding and border. Without it, a width: 100% box with padding is wider than its parent and overflows. Every modern site uses this. body { margin: 0; } Removes the browser's default 8 px gap around the page. font-family: system-ui, … Uses the phone's or computer's own font (San Francisco on Apple, Segoe UI on Windows, Roboto on Android): fast, because there's nothing to download. font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.5; 16 px is the readable minimum for body text. line-height: 1.5 (no unit) means 1.5 × the font size. color / background Use the tokens, so the whole page follows them. img { display: block; max-width: 100%; } Images never overflow their box, and lose the small gap below them that inline images have. button, input, select { font: inherit; } Form controls don't inherit the page font by default; this fixes it. a { color: inherit; } Links take the colour of the text around them; we colour them ourselves where needed. [hidden] { display: none !important; } A real bug we hit while building this page. The hidden attribute hides an element only through the browser's own display: none. Our .btn { display: inline-flex } is more specific, so a "hidden" ADD button stayed visible. This one rule makes hidden always win.

docs.title: Shared helpers
Try it
docs.text:
1. Change --brand to #7c3aed and reload. Every button and the logo turn purple.
  2. Delete the viewport <meta> line, open DevTools device mode (Ctrl+Shift+M) and see how tiny the text gets. Put it back.
  3. Remove box-sizing: border-box, give .container a padding: 20px, and watch it overflow the screen on a phone.

docs.title: Solutions
docs.text:
Try each exercise yourself first, then open its solution to compare.

1. Change the brand colour

Edit the one token in css/base.css:

:root {
  --brand: #7c3aed;   /* was #0c831f */
}

The logo, every .btn, the outline buttons' border and text, and the price filter's checkboxes (accent-color) all turn purple, because they all read var(--brand). --brand-dark (hover) and --brand-soft (pale backgrounds) are separate tokens: for a complete re-brand, change those too, for example #5b21b6 and #ede9fe.

2. Remove the viewport meta tag

Without <meta name="viewport" …>, a phone lays the page out at about 980 px wide (a pretend desktop) and then shrinks the whole thing to fit its screen. You see a tiny, zoomed-out page: text around 6–7 px, buttons too small to tap, and no media query for phones ever matches, because the page thinks it's 980 px wide. Put the line back and everything is normal size again.

3. Remove box-sizing: border-box

With the default box-sizing: content-box, width means the content only, and padding is added on top:

content-box (default) border-box .container width on a 375 px phone min(100% - 32px, 1200px) = 343 px 343 px + padding: 20px (left + right) 343 + 40 = 383 px stays 343 px (padding goes inside) Result 8 px wider than the 375 px screen → sideways scroll fits

That's why every modern reset starts with *, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Forgetting the viewport meta tag: the "responsive" site looks like a shrunken desktop on phones.
  • Hard-coding #0c831f in 40 places instead of using a token, then needing to change the brand colour.
  • Using <div onclick> instead of <button>: no keyboard support, no screen-reader role.
  • Using headings for size (<h4> because it's small). Choose the level by structure and set the size in CSS.

docs.title: 2. Header & Category Nav
docs.text:
Beginner Intermediate

The header is the most-used part of any store: people search, check their cart and switch categories from it. It is made of five small components: announcement bar, logo + location, search box, actions (login + cart with a count badge) and the category nav underneath.

docs.title: What you see
docs.text:
Open it full-size: 02-header.html and make the window narrow: the search box drops to its own row and the category nav becomes swipeable.

Phone (< 768 px)Desktop (≥ 768 px) 
┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
│ FreshCart  Delivery in 10…   [🛒 Cart 3]│  row 1: logo · location · actions
│ [ Search for milk, bread…        🔍 ] │  row 2: search spans all columns
├───────────────────────────────────────┤
│ (All) Fruits Vegetables Dairy Bak… →  │  swipe sideways
└───────────────────────────────────────┘

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ FreshCart  Delivery in 10 min  [ Search for milk…          🔍 ]  Login [🛒 Cart 3] │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ (All)  Fruits  Vegetables  Dairy & Eggs  Bakery  Snacks  Beverages  …           │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: ① Skip link and announcement bar
docs.text:
<a class="visually-hidden skip-link" href="#main">Skip to main content</a>

<p class="announcement">
  Free delivery on orders above ₹199. <a href="#offers">See today's offers</a>
</p>

.announcement {
  background: var(--text);
  color: #fff;
  font-size: 0.85rem;
  text-align: center;
  padding: var(--space-2) var(--space-4);
}
.announcement a {
  color: var(--accent);
  font-weight: 600;
}
Code What it does <a class="visually-hidden skip-link" href="#main"> The first thing a keyboard user reaches. Pressing Enter jumps past the header to <main id="main">. Invisible until focused (see lesson 1). <p class="announcement"> A one-line promotional strip. It's just a paragraph; no special element is needed. <a href="#offers"> Links to the element with id="offers" on the same page (the offers row in lesson 3). background: var(--text); color: #fff; Dark strip, white text: it stands apart from the white header. font-size: 0.85rem; rem is relative to the root font size (16 px), so 0.85 rem ≈ 13.6 px. It scales if the user enlarges text in their browser. .announcement a { color: var(--accent); } The link is yellow so it stands out on dark.

docs.title: ② The header shell: one grid, two layouts
docs.text:
<header class="site-header">
  <div class="container header-inner">
    <a class="logo" href="#" aria-label="FreshCart home">Fresh<span>Cart</span></a>

    <div class="location">
      <strong>Delivery in 10 minutes</strong>
      <span>Home: 21 MG Road, Bengaluru</span>
    </div>

    <form class="search" role="search" action="#">
      <label class="visually-hidden" for="q">Search products</label>
      <input id="q" name="q" type="search" placeholder="Search for milk, bread, apples…">
      <button type="submit" aria-label="Search">🔍</button>
    </form>

    <div class="header-actions">
      <a class="account-link" href="#">Login</a>
      <button class="btn cart-button" type="button" data-open-cart aria-label="Open cart">
        🛒 <span class="cart-label">Cart</span>
        <span class="cart-count" data-cart-count aria-hidden="true">0</span>
      </button>
    </div>
  </div>
</header>
Line(s) What it does <header class="site-header"> The banner landmark. The class is for styling, so we don't style the bare header tag (there can be other headers, e.g. inside articles). <div class="container header-inner"> Two classes: container limits the width (lesson 1), header-inner is the grid we define below. <a class="logo" href="#" aria-label="FreshCart home"> The logo always links home. aria-label gives screen readers a clear name ("FreshCart home") instead of reading the two spans separately. Fresh<span>Cart</span> The <span> lets us colour "Cart" differently. <div class="location"> with <strong> and <span> Two lines of text: delivery promise (bold) and the address (grey). <form class="search" role="search" action="#"> A real form, so Enter submits it. role="search" makes it a search landmark. action is where it submits (a results URL in a real store). <label class="visually-hidden" for="q"> Every input needs a label. The design shows no label, so we hide it visually; screen readers still read "Search products". for="q" connects it to id="q". <input id="q" name="q" type="search" placeholder="…"> type="search" gives a clear (×) button on some browsers and a "search" key on phone keyboards. name="q" becomes ?q=apples in the URL. The placeholder is a hint, never a replacement for the label. <button type="submit" aria-label="Search">🔍</button> The emoji alone isn't a good accessible name, so aria-label provides one. <div class="header-actions"> A flex row for Login and Cart. <a class="account-link" href="#">Login</a> Hidden on phones (the bottom nav has Account), shown on desktop. <button class="btn cart-button" type="button" data-open-cart …> type="button" (not submit). data-open-cart is a data attribute: a hook for JavaScript (lesson 6). We select by data attributes in JS and by classes in CSS so a CSS rename never breaks JS. <span class="cart-count" data-cart-count aria-hidden="true">0</span> The red badge. JavaScript updates the number. aria-hidden stops screen readers reading "0" separately: the button's aria-label ("Open cart, 3 items") already includes it. 
.site-header {
  position: sticky;
  top: 0;
  z-index: 10;
  background: var(--surface);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line);
}

.header-inner {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto;
  grid-template-areas:
    "logo   location actions"
    "search search   search";
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--space-3) var(--space-4);
  padding-block: var(--space-3);
}

.logo           { grid-area: logo; }
.location       { grid-area: location; }
.search         { grid-area: search; }
.header-actions { grid-area: actions; }

@media (width >= 768px) {
  .header-inner {
    grid-template-columns: auto auto 1fr auto;
    grid-template-areas: "logo location search actions";
  }
}
Code What it does position: sticky; top: 0; The header scrolls normally until it hits the top of the screen, then sticks there. z-index: 10; Keeps the header above the products that scroll underneath it. border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line); A thin line separates the header from the page. display: grid; header-inner becomes a grid container. grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto; Phone: three columns. Logo and actions take only the space they need (auto); the location gets the rest (1fr = one fraction of the leftover space). grid-template-areas: "logo location actions" "search search search"; Draws the layout as text. Each string is a row; each word is a cell. Writing search three times makes the search box span all three columns on row 2. align-items: center; Vertically centres every item in its row. gap: var(--space-3) var(--space-4); 12 px between rows, 16 px between columns. padding-block: var(--space-3); Padding on the top and bottom only (block = vertical in horizontal writing). .logo { grid-area: logo; } … Places each child into the named area. The HTML order doesn't have to match the visual order. @media (width >= 768px) { … } On screens at least 768 px wide (tablets and up)… grid-template-columns: auto auto 1fr auto; …four columns: logo, location, search (takes all spare space), actions… grid-template-areas: "logo location search actions"; …all in a single row. Only the grid changes; the HTML stays the same.

docs.title: ③ Logo and location
docs.text:
.logo {
  font-size: 1.5rem;
  font-weight: 800;
  color: var(--brand);
  text-decoration: none;
  letter-spacing: -0.02em;
}
.logo span {
  color: var(--accent);
}

.location {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  min-width: 0;
  font-size: 0.8rem;
  line-height: 1.2;
}
.location strong {
  font-size: 0.9rem;
}
.location span {
  color: var(--muted);
  white-space: nowrap;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
}
Code What it does font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: -0.02em; A heavy, slightly tight wordmark: a text logo with no image file. .logo span { color: var(--accent); } "Cart" in yellow. .location { display: flex; flex-direction: column; } Stacks the two lines vertically. min-width: 0; Important. Grid and flex items refuse to shrink below their content's width by default. min-width: 0 lets this item shrink so the address can be cut off instead of pushing the cart off-screen. white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; The classic three-line "cut off with …" pattern. All three are required.

docs.title: ④ Search box
docs.text:
.search {
  display: flex;
  border: 1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
  background: var(--page);
  overflow: hidden;
}
.search:focus-within {
  border-color: var(--brand);
  outline: 2px solid var(--brand-soft);
}
.search input {
  flex: 1;
  min-width: 0;
  border: 0;
  padding: var(--space-2) var(--space-3);
  background: transparent;
}
.search input:focus {
  outline: none;
}
.search button {
  border: 0;
  padding-inline: var(--space-4);
  background: var(--brand);
  color: #fff;
  cursor: pointer;
}
Code What it does .search { display: flex; } Input and button side by side. overflow: hidden; + border-radius The button's square corners are clipped to the form's rounded corners. .search:focus-within Matches the form when anything inside it has focus, so the whole box gets a green border while typing. .search input { flex: 1; min-width: 0; } The input grows to fill the space; min-width: 0 lets it shrink on tiny screens (inputs have a built-in minimum width otherwise). border: 0; background: transparent; The input blends into the form, which draws the border. .search input:focus { outline: none; } Safe here only because :focus-within on the form already shows a visible focus style. padding-inline: var(--space-4); Left and right padding on the search button.

docs.title: ⑤ Actions and the cart badge
docs.text:
.header-actions {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--space-2);
}

.account-link {
  display: none;
  text-decoration: none;
  font-weight: 600;
  padding: var(--space-2);
}
@media (width >= 768px) {
  .account-link {
    display: inline-block;
  }
}

.cart-button {
  position: relative;
}
.cart-count {
  position: absolute;
  top: -8px;
  right: -8px;
  min-width: 22px;
  height: 22px;
  padding-inline: 6px;
  border-radius: 999px;
  border: 2px solid var(--surface);
  background: var(--danger);
  color: #fff;
  font-size: 0.75rem;
  line-height: 18px;
  text-align: center;
}
Code What it does .header-actions { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: … } Login and Cart in a row, vertically centred, 8 px apart. .account-link { display: none; } then display: inline-block at ≥ 768 px Mobile first: hidden by default, shown on wider screens. .cart-button { position: relative; } Makes the button the reference box for the badge's absolute position. .cart-count { position: absolute; top: -8px; right: -8px; } Pins the badge to the button's top-right corner, overlapping it by 8 px. min-width: 22px; height: 22px; border-radius: 999px; A circle for one digit that grows into a pill for "12". A huge radius always gives fully round ends. border: 2px solid var(--surface); A white ring that separates the badge from the green button. line-height: 18px; text-align: center; Centres the digit: 22 px height − 2 × 2 px border = 18 px inside.

docs.title: ⑥ Category nav: a row that scrolls sideways
docs.text:
<nav class="category-nav" aria-label="Categories">
  <ul class="container">
    <li><a href="#" aria-current="page">All</a></li>
    <li><a href="#">Fruits</a></li>
    <li><a href="#">Vegetables</a></li>
    <li><a href="#">Dairy & Eggs</a></li>
    <li><a href="#">Bakery</a></li>
    <li><a href="#">Snacks</a></li>
    <li><a href="#">Beverages</a></li>
    <li><a href="#">Household</a></li>
    <li><a href="#">Personal care</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>

.category-nav {
  background: var(--surface);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line);
}
.category-nav ul {
  display: flex;
  gap: var(--space-2);
  margin: 0;
  padding: var(--space-2) 0;
  list-style: none;
  overflow-x: auto;
  scrollbar-width: none;
  scroll-snap-type: x proximity;
}
.category-nav a {
  display: block;
  padding: var(--space-1) var(--space-3);
  border-radius: 999px;
  white-space: nowrap;
  text-decoration: none;
  font-size: 0.9rem;
  scroll-snap-align: start;
}
.category-nav a:hover,
.category-nav a[aria-current="page"] {
  background: var(--brand-soft);
  color: var(--brand-dark);
  font-weight: 600;
}
Code What it does <nav aria-label="Categories"> A navigation landmark. The label tells it apart from the footer and bottom navs. <ul class="container"> Links are a list: screen readers announce "list, 9 items". aria-current="page" Marks the link for the current page. We style it from this attribute, so the look and the accessibility can't drift apart. display: flex; gap: var(--space-2); Links in one row with 8 px gaps. margin: 0; padding: … 0; list-style: none; Removes the list's default bullets and indentation. overflow-x: auto; When the links don't fit (on phones), the row scrolls sideways instead of wrapping or overflowing the page. scrollbar-width: none; Hides the scrollbar; touch users swipe. scroll-snap-type: x proximity; + scroll-snap-align: start; After a swipe, the row settles so a link lines up with the left edge. white-space: nowrap; "Dairy & Eggs" stays on one line. border-radius: 999px; Pill-shaped highlight for hover and the current page.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
1. Change the phone layout so the search box is on row 1 and the location on row 2. You only need to edit grid-template-areas.
  2. Make the cart badge show "9+" when the count is more than 9 (hint: JavaScript in lesson 6).
  3. Add a "Deals 🔥" link to the category nav with a red text colour.

docs.title: Solutions
docs.text:
Try each exercise yourself first, then open its solution to compare.

Every code solution below is applied in store-solved.html: the full store with all the exercises from every lesson done, tested in a real browser like the original. Its files are generated from store.html and store.js, so the snippets here are exactly what runs there.

1. Search on row 1, location on row 2

Only the grid areas change. Because this rule lives in a stylesheet that loads after header.css, it also has to repeat the desktop layout, or it would win on desktop too:

/* Lesson 2, exercise 1: on phones, search on row 1 and the location on row 2 */
.header-inner {
  grid-template-areas:
    "logo     search   actions"
    "location location location";
}
/* This file loads after header.css, so the rule above would also beat header.css's desktop layout.
   Repeat the desktop areas here to win back the one-row header from 768 px. */
@media (width >= 768px) {
  .header-inner {
    grid-template-areas: "logo location search actions";
  }
}
/* Sharing row 1 with the logo and the cart leaves the search box very narrow on small phones (that's why the
   original design gives it its own row). Hiding the word "Cart" wins back ~45 px; the button keeps its aria-label. */
@media (width < 480px) {
  .cart-label {
    display: none;
  }
}

It works, but look at it on a 375 px phone: the search box now shares the row with the logo and the cart, so it's only about 140 px wide, even after hiding the word "Cart". That's the reason the original design gives search a full row of its own. Moving things around is easy with grid-template-areas; deciding where they fit best is the real design work.

2. Show “9+” in the cart badge

In render(), replace the line that writes the count into the badge:

// A two-digit number doesn't fit in the round badge, so cap what it shows
const badgeText = count > 9 ? "9+" : String(count);
document.querySelectorAll("[data-cart-count]").forEach((badge) => (badge.textContent = badgeText));

String(count) keeps both branches the same type (text). The full number is still in the button's aria-label ("Open cart, 12 items"), so screen-reader users lose nothing.

3. A red “Deals 🔥” link 
<li><a class="deals-link" href="#">Deals 🔥</a></li>

/* Lesson 2, exercise 3: a red "Deals" link */
.category-nav a.deals-link {
  color: var(--danger);
  font-weight: 700;
}

a.deals-link (an element plus a class) is more specific than .category-nav a, so its colour wins. Red text on white (#d6342c) has a contrast of about 4.8 : 1, which passes WCAG AA for normal text.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Building the header with floats or fixed pixel widths, so it breaks at in-between screen sizes.
  • Using a placeholder instead of a <label>: the hint disappears as soon as you type, and screen readers may skip it.
  • Forgetting min-width: 0, so a long address pushes the cart button off-screen.
  • position: fixed instead of sticky: a fixed header covers the top of the content and you need to add padding to compensate.

docs.title: 3. Hero, Offers & Category Tiles
docs.text:
Beginner

The top of the home page sells the store: a big hero banner with one clear button, a row of offer cards, and category tiles that are shortcuts into the catalogue.

docs.title: What you see
docs.text: Open it full-size: 03-hero.html. At phone width the picture disappears and the offers become a swipeable carousel.

docs.title: ⑦ Hero banner and ⑧ offers: HTML
docs.text:
<section class="hero" aria-labelledby="hero-title">
  <div>
    <h1 id="hero-title">Fresh groceries at your door in 10 minutes</h1>
    <p>Fruit, vegetables, dairy and daily essentials, picked fresh from local farms every morning.</p>
    <a class="btn" href="#shop">Shop now</a>
  </div>
  <div class="hero-art" aria-hidden="true">🥦🍎</div>
</section>

<ul class="offers" id="offers" aria-label="Offers">
  <li><strong>Flat 50% off</strong> on your first order</li>
  <li><strong>Buy 1 get 1</strong> on all bakery items</li>
  <li><strong>₹100 cashback</strong> with UPI payments</li>
</ul>
Code What it does <section class="hero" aria-labelledby="hero-title"> A <section> is a themed group of content. aria-labelledby names it after its heading, so screen-reader users hear "Fresh groceries at your door, region". <div> (first child) Groups the text so it's one grid cell (heading + paragraph + button together). <h1 id="hero-title"> The page's single h1. The id is what aria-labelledby points at. <a class="btn" href="#shop">Shop now</a> One call to action. Jumps to the product section further down. <div class="hero-art" aria-hidden="true">🥦🍎</div> Decoration only. aria-hidden stops screen readers reading "broccoli, red apple". <ul class="offers" id="offers" aria-label="Offers"> Three offers are a list. The id is the target of the announcement-bar link. <li><strong>Flat 50% off</strong> on your first order</li> <strong> for the important part; CSS puts it on its own line.

docs.title: Hero: CSS
docs.text:
.hero {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--space-4);
  margin-top: var(--space-4);
  padding: var(--space-6);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  background: linear-gradient(120deg, #e3f5e1 0%, #fff6d8 100%);
}
.hero h1 {
  margin: 0 0 var(--space-2);
  font-size: clamp(1.6rem, 1.1rem + 2.5vw, 2.75rem);
  line-height: 1.1;
}
.hero p {
  margin: 0 0 var(--space-4);
  color: var(--muted);
  max-width: 45ch;
}
.hero-art {
  display: none;
  font-size: 7rem;
  text-align: center;
  line-height: 1;
}
@media (width >= 768px) {
  .hero {
    grid-template-columns: 1.4fr 1fr;
    padding: var(--space-8);
  }
  .hero-art {
    display: block;
  }
}
Code What it does display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr; Phone: one column, so the text fills the width. align-items: center; On desktop, text and picture are vertically centred against each other. margin-top, padding, border-radius Spacing from the tokens; rounded corners make it read as a card. background: linear-gradient(120deg, #e3f5e1 0%, #fff6d8 100%); A soft diagonal fade from mint to cream. 120deg is the direction; the percentages say where each colour is fully reached. No image file needed. font-size: clamp(1.6rem, 1.1rem + 2.5vw, 2.75rem); Fluid type. clamp(MIN, PREFERRED, MAX). The preferred size grows with the viewport width (vw = 1 % of the window width), but never goes below 1.6 rem or above 2.75 rem. One line replaces several media queries. line-height: 1.1; Big headings look better with tight line spacing. max-width: 45ch; ch ≈ the width of the "0" character. About 45–75 characters per line is comfortable to read. .hero-art { display: none; } Mobile first: no picture on small screens. It costs space and adds nothing. @media (width >= 768px) → grid-template-columns: 1.4fr 1fr; On wider screens: two columns, the text column 1.4 × as wide as the picture column. .hero-art { display: block; } …and the picture appears.

docs.title: Offers: a carousel with no JavaScript
docs.text:
.offers {
  display: grid;
  grid-auto-flow: column;
  grid-auto-columns: 80%;
  gap: var(--space-4);
  margin: var(--space-4) 0 0;
  padding: 0 0 var(--space-2);
  list-style: none;
  overflow-x: auto;
  scroll-snap-type: x mandatory;
}
.offers li {
  scroll-snap-align: start;
  padding: var(--space-4);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  color: #fff;
}
.offers li:nth-child(1) { background: #2563eb; }
.offers li:nth-child(2) { background: #db2777; }
.offers li:nth-child(3) { background: #7c3aed; }
.offers strong {
  display: block;
  font-size: 1.1rem;
}
@media (width >= 768px) {
  .offers {
    grid-auto-flow: row;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
    overflow: visible;
  }
}
Code What it does display: grid; grid-auto-flow: column; Every item goes into a new column instead of a new row, so they line up horizontally. grid-auto-columns: 80%; Each card is 80 % of the container: the next card peeks in from the right, which tells the user "swipe me". list-style: none; margin; padding Resets the <ul>. The bottom padding leaves room for the scrollbar on desktop browsers. overflow-x: auto; The row scrolls sideways. scroll-snap-type: x mandatory; + scroll-snap-align: start; After a swipe, it always stops with a card aligned to the left edge, like an app carousel. li:nth-child(1) { background: #2563eb; } Picks the 1st, 2nd and 3rd item to give each a different colour. strong { display: block; } <strong> is inline by default; block puts it on its own line. @media (width >= 768px) Desktop: back to normal rows (grid-auto-flow: row), three equal columns, no scrolling.

docs.title: ⑨ Category tiles
docs.text:
<section class="section" aria-labelledby="cat-title">
  <div class="section-head">
    <h2 id="cat-title">Shop by category</h2>
    <a href="#">See all</a>
  </div>
  <ul class="category-grid">
    <li><a class="category-tile" href="#"><span class="category-icon" aria-hidden="true">🍎</span>Fruits</a></li>
    <li><a class="category-tile" href="#"><span class="category-icon" aria-hidden="true">🥕</span>Vegetables</a></li>
    <li><a class="category-tile" href="#"><span class="category-icon" aria-hidden="true">🥛</span>Dairy & Eggs</a></li>
    <li><a class="category-tile" href="#"><span class="category-icon" aria-hidden="true">🍞</span>Bakery</a></li>
    <li><a class="category-tile" href="#"><span class="category-icon" aria-hidden="true">🍪</span>Snacks</a></li>
    <li><a class="category-tile" href="#"><span class="category-icon" aria-hidden="true">🧃</span>Beverages</a></li>
  </ul>
</section>

.section {
  padding-block: var(--space-6);
}
.section-head {
  display: flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: var(--space-4);
  margin-bottom: var(--space-4);
}
.section-head h2 {
  margin: 0;
  font-size: clamp(1.15rem, 1rem + 1vw, 1.5rem);
}
.section-head a {
  color: var(--brand);
  font-weight: 600;
  text-decoration: none;
  white-space: nowrap;
}

.category-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(96px, 1fr));
  gap: var(--space-3);
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  list-style: none;
}
.category-tile {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--space-2);
  padding: var(--space-3) var(--space-2);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  background: var(--surface);
  text-align: center;
  text-decoration: none;
  font-size: 0.85rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  line-height: 1.2;
  transition: transform 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s;
}
.category-tile:hover {
  transform: translateY(-2px);
  box-shadow: var(--shadow);
}
.category-icon {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  width: 64px;
  aspect-ratio: 1;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--brand-soft);
  font-size: 2rem;
}
Code What it does <div class="section-head"> with <h2> and <a>See all</a> A reusable section heading component: title left, link right. Used again in lesson 5. .section-head { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: baseline; } Pushes the title and link to opposite ends; baseline lines up the bottoms of their letters even though the fonts differ in size. <ul class="category-grid"> + <li><a class="category-tile"> A list of links. The whole tile is the link, so it's a big tap target. <span class="category-icon" aria-hidden="true">🍎</span>Fruits Icon is decoration; the link's name is just "Fruits". grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(96px, 1fr)); The responsive-grid one-liner. "Make as many columns as fit, each at least 96 px, and share the leftover space equally." 3 per row on a phone, 6+ on a desktop, no media queries. .category-tile { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; } Icon above text, both centred. transition: transform 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s; Animates the hover change instead of jumping. .category-tile:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: … } Lifts the tile 2 px and adds a shadow. transform is cheap for the browser to animate. .category-icon { display: grid; place-items: center; } The shortest way to centre something both ways. width: 64px; aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 50%; A 64 × 64 circle. aspect-ratio: 1 keeps height equal to width.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
1. Change minmax(96px, 1fr) to minmax(140px, 1fr) and watch fewer, wider tiles appear.
  2. Change the offers' 80% to 45% so two cards fit on a phone.
  3. Replace the hero gradient with a photo: background: url(img/hero.jpg) center / cover; and make sure the text stays readable.

docs.title: Solutions
docs.text:
Try each exercise yourself first, then open its solution to compare.

1. minmax(96px, 1fr) → minmax(140px, 1fr)

Each tile must now be at least 140 px wide, so fewer fit in a row:

Container width minmax(96px, 1fr) minmax(140px, 1fr) 343 px (375 px phone) 3 per row 2 per row 1200 px (desktop) 11 tracks (6 tiles + 5 empty ones) 7 tracks (6 tiles + 1 empty)

With only 6 tiles, auto-fill keeps the empty tracks, so on a desktop the tiles stay small and sit on the left. Switch to auto-fit if you want the 6 tiles to stretch and fill the row instead.

2. Offers at 45% so two fit on a phone 
.offers {
  grid-auto-columns: 45%;
}

Two cards (2 × 45% + one 16 px gap) fit in the 343 px row, and a sliver of the third still peeks in, so people know they can swipe. On wider screens nothing changes, because the @media (width >= 768px) rule switches the offers to three normal columns.

3. A photo behind the hero text 
.hero {
  background:
    linear-gradient(90deg, rgb(255 255 255 / 0.95) 0%, rgb(255 255 255 / 0.6) 60%, transparent 100%),
    url(img/hero.jpg) center / cover;
}
Code Why Two backgrounds, separated by a comma The first one is drawn on top. The white linear-gradient A see-through white layer behind the text keeps it readable on any photo. Without it, dark text on a busy photo fails contrast checks. center / cover Centre the photo and scale it to cover the whole box, cropping the edges if needed.

This needs an image file, so it isn't applied in the solved store. Always check the text contrast after adding a photo (DevTools → Inspect the heading → the colour picker shows the contrast ratio).

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• A hero with three buttons and four messages. One headline, one sentence, one button.
  • font-size: 48px on the hero heading: huge on phones. Use clamp().
  • A JavaScript slider library for three offer cards. CSS scroll snap does it with no JS, and it's smooth on touch screens.
  • Making only the icon a link. Wrap the whole tile in the <a> so the tap target is large.

docs.title: 4. Product Card & Product Grid
docs.text:
Beginner Intermediate

The product card is the most important component in e-commerce: it's repeated hundreds of times and it's where people decide to buy. Ours has six small parts, and the ADD button turns into a − 1 + quantity stepper once the item is in the cart.

docs.title: What you see
docs.text: Click ADD, then + and −. Open it full-size: 04-product-card.html.

docs.title: Anatomy of one card
docs.text:
🍎 20% OFF ⏱ 10 MINS Shimla Apple 1 kg ₹189₹236 ADD
  1. Media: the product picture, a perfect square.
  2. Badge: floats over the picture's corner.
  3. Text: delivery time, name (max 2 lines), pack size.
  4. Footer: price on the left, ADD button on the right, always at the bottom of the card.
  5. Stepper: replaces ADD once the item is in the cart.
  6. Card + grid: the white box, and the grid that arranges many cards.

docs.title: The HTML of one card
docs.text:
<article class="product-card" data-id="apple" data-name="Shimla Apple" data-price="18900" data-category="fruits" data-deal>
  <div class="product-media" role="img" aria-label="Red apples">🍎</div>
  <span class="badge">20% OFF</span>
  <p class="product-eta">⏱ 10 MINS</p>
  <h3 class="product-title">Shimla Apple</h3>
  <p class="product-size">1 kg</p>
  <div class="product-footer">
    <p class="price"><strong>₹189</strong> <s>₹236</s></p>
    <button class="btn btn--outline add-btn" type="button" data-add>ADD</button>
    <div class="qty" hidden>
      <button type="button" data-dec aria-label="Remove one Shimla Apple">−</button>
      <output aria-live="polite">0</output>
      <button type="button" data-inc aria-label="Add one more Shimla Apple">+</button>
    </div>
  </div>
</article>
Code What it does <article class="product-card" …> <article> = a self-contained item that would make sense on its own (like a tweet or a product). data-id="apple" A unique id. JavaScript uses it as the key in the cart. data-name="Shimla Apple" The name the cart drawer shows. data-price="18900" The price in paise (₹189.00 = 18900). Money is stored as a whole number so adding prices never produces 0.30000000000000004. data-category="fruits" and data-deal Used by the filters in lesson 5. data-deal has no value: its presence alone means "this is discounted". <div class="product-media" role="img" aria-label="Red apples">🍎</div> Stands in for the photo. role="img" + aria-label make screen readers treat it as an image called "Red apples". <span class="badge">20% OFF</span> The discount badge. CSS positions it over the picture. <p class="product-eta">⏱ 10 MINS</p> Delivery time. <h3 class="product-title"> The product name is a heading, so screen-reader users can jump from product to product with the H key. It's h3 because the section title is h2. <p class="product-size">1 kg</p> Pack size. <div class="product-footer"> Groups price and button so CSS can put them side by side. <p class="price"><strong>₹189</strong> <s>₹236</s></p> <s> means "no longer accurate", the correct element for an old price. <button class="btn btn--outline add-btn" type="button" data-add>ADD</button> A real <button>: keyboard and screen readers work for free. data-add is the JavaScript hook. <div class="qty" hidden> The stepper. The hidden attribute hides it until the item is in the cart. <button … data-dec aria-label="Remove one Shimla Apple">−</button> A "−" alone means nothing to a screen reader, so the label says exactly what it does and to which product. <output aria-live="polite">0</output> <output> is the element for a calculated value. aria-live="polite" makes screen readers announce the new number when it changes.

docs.title: In a real store: the image
docs.text:
Replace the emoji <div> with a real image like this:

<img class="product-media" src="img/apple-400.webp"
     srcset="img/apple-200.webp 200w, img/apple-400.webp 400w"
     sizes="(width >= 768px) 200px, 45vw"
     width="400" height="400" alt="Shimla apples, 1 kg pack"
     loading="lazy" decoding="async">
Attribute Why src / srcset / sizes The browser picks the smallest file that looks sharp on this screen, so phones download less. width / height The browser reserves the space before the image loads, so the page doesn't jump (CLS, a Core Web Vital). alt Describes the image for screen readers and when it fails to load. loading="lazy" Loads the image only when it's about to scroll into view. Don't use it on images visible at the top of the page.

docs.title: Card and grid: CSS
docs.text:
.product-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(160px, 100%), 1fr));
  gap: var(--space-3);
}
@media (width >= 768px) {
  .product-grid {
    grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(190px, 1fr));
    gap: var(--space-4);
  }
}

.product-card {
  position: relative;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  padding: var(--space-3);
  border: 1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  background: var(--surface);
  transition: box-shadow 0.15s;
}
.product-card:hover {
  box-shadow: var(--shadow);
}
Code What it does grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(160px, 100%), 1fr)); As many columns as fit, each at least 160 px: 2 cards per row on a phone. min(160px, 100%) prevents overflow on a very narrow screen. gap: var(--space-3); 12 px between cards. @media (width >= 768px) → minmax(190px, 1fr), bigger gap Slightly larger cards on desktop: 4–5 per row. .product-card { position: relative; } The reference box for the absolutely positioned badge. display: flex; flex-direction: column; Stacks the parts vertically. This is what lets the footer sit at the bottom (see margin-top: auto below). border, border-radius, background The white rounded box. transition: box-shadow 0.15s; + :hover { box-shadow } A soft lift on hover. 
.product-media {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  aspect-ratio: 1;
  margin-bottom: var(--space-2);
  border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
  background: var(--page);
  font-size: 3.5rem;
}

.badge {
  position: absolute;
  top: var(--space-3);
  left: var(--space-3);
  padding: 2px var(--space-2);
  border-radius: var(--space-1);
  background: #2563eb;
  color: #fff;
  font-size: 0.7rem;
  font-weight: 700;
}
Code What it does display: grid; place-items: center; Centres the emoji (or a smaller product photo) in the box. aspect-ratio: 1; A perfect square at any card width. All pictures line up even if the source photos have different shapes. With a real <img>, add object-fit: contain so the photo isn't stretched. .badge { position: absolute; top: …; left: …; } Takes the badge out of the normal flow and pins it 12 px from the card's top-left corner, over the picture. font-size: 0.7rem; font-weight: 700; Small, bold text. 
.product-eta {
  margin: 0;
  font-size: 0.7rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  color: var(--muted);
}
.product-title {
  margin: var(--space-1) 0;
  font-size: 0.95rem;
  line-height: 1.3;
  display: -webkit-box;
  -webkit-line-clamp: 2;
  -webkit-box-orient: vertical;
  overflow: hidden;
}
.product-size {
  margin: 0 0 var(--space-3);
  color: var(--muted);
  font-size: 0.85rem;
}
Code What it does .product-eta { font-size: 0.7rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--muted); } Small grey label. display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 2; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden; Line clamp: show at most 2 lines and end with "…". Long names ("Brown Eggs, farm fresh and free range") don't make one card taller than the rest. The -webkit- prefix is still needed; every modern browser supports it. margin: 0 0 var(--space-3); Space below the pack size, before the footer. 
.product-footer {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: var(--space-2);
  margin-top: auto;
}
.price {
  margin: 0;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  line-height: 1.2;
  font-size: 0.9rem;
}
.price s {
  color: var(--muted);
  font-size: 0.8rem;
}
.add-btn {
  min-width: 72px;
  padding-block: 6px;
}
Code What it does .product-footer { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; } Price on the left, button on the right, vertically centred. margin-top: auto; The trick that aligns every ADD button. In a flex column, an auto margin takes all the free space, so it pushes the footer to the bottom of the card. Cards in a row are equal height (grid stretches them), so all the buttons line up. .price { display: flex; flex-direction: column; } New price above old price. .add-btn { min-width: 72px; } ADD and the stepper are the same width, so nothing shifts when one replaces the other. 
.qty {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  min-width: 72px;
  border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
  background: var(--brand);
  color: #fff;
  font-weight: 700;
}
.qty button {
  width: 26px;
  height: 34px;
  border: 0;
  background: none;
  color: inherit;
  font-size: 1.1rem;
  cursor: pointer;
}
.qty output {
  flex: 1;
  text-align: center;
}
Code What it does .qty { display: inline-flex; min-width: 72px; background: var(--brand); color: #fff; } A green pill holding − n +. .qty button { width: 26px; height: 34px; border: 0; background: none; color: inherit; } Strips the default button look so only the symbol shows, in white. .qty output { flex: 1; text-align: center; } The number takes the space between the two buttons.

docs.title: The JavaScript: ADD, +, −
docs.text:
The full script is in js/store.js; these are the parts this card uses.

// The single source of truth: product id -> { name, price, qty }.
// Every change goes through setQty(), which then redraws the UI from this Map.
const cart = new Map();

function setQty(card, qty) {
  const { id, name, price } = card.dataset;
  if (qty <= 0) cart.delete(id);
  else cart.set(id, { name, price: Number(price), qty });
  render();
}
Code What it does const cart = new Map(); The state: a Map from product id to { name, price, qty }. Everything on screen is drawn from this one object. function setQty(card, qty) The only function that changes the cart. Having one door in makes bugs easy to find. const { id, name, price } = card.dataset; dataset reads the data-* attributes: data-id → dataset.id. Destructuring pulls three at once. if (qty <= 0) cart.delete(id); Quantity 0 means "remove from cart". else cart.set(id, { name, price: Number(price), qty }); Data attributes are always strings; Number() converts "18900" to 18900. render(); Redraw the screen from the new state. 
// One listener on the grid handles every button in every card (event delegation).
const grid = document.querySelector("[data-product-grid]");

grid?.addEventListener("click", (event) => {
  const button = event.target.closest("button");
  if (!button) return;
  const card = button.closest(".product-card");
  const current = cart.get(card.dataset.id)?.qty ?? 0;

  if (button.matches("[data-add], [data-inc]")) setQty(card, current + 1);
  if (button.matches("[data-dec]")) setQty(card, current - 1);

  // After "ADD" turns into the stepper, keep keyboard focus on the "+" button.
  if (button.matches("[data-add]")) card.querySelector("[data-inc]").focus();
});
Code What it does document.querySelector("[data-product-grid]") Finds the grid by its data attribute. grid?.addEventListener("click", …) Event delegation: one listener on the grid instead of 24 on every button. It still works for cards added later (e.g. infinite scroll). ?. skips this if the page has no grid. event.target.closest("button") The click might land on the button or on text inside it; closest() walks up to the nearest <button>. if (!button) return; The click was on the card but not on a button: do nothing. button.closest(".product-card") Which product was clicked. cart.get(card.dataset.id)?.qty ?? 0 Current quantity, or 0 if it's not in the cart (?. avoids an error on undefined, ?? supplies the default). button.matches("[data-add], [data-inc]") Was it ADD or +? Then add one. button.matches("[data-dec]") Was it −? Then remove one. card.querySelector("[data-inc]").focus(); ADD disappears when clicked, which would leave keyboard focus nowhere. Moving focus to "+" keeps keyboard users in place. 
function render() {
  // 1. Each card shows "ADD" when it is not in the cart, and the − n + stepper when it is.
  document.querySelectorAll(".product-card").forEach((card) => {
    const qty = cart.get(card.dataset.id)?.qty ?? 0;
    card.querySelector("[data-add]").hidden = qty > 0;
    card.querySelector(".qty").hidden = qty === 0;
    card.querySelector("output").textContent = qty;
  });

  // 2. The red badge on the cart button.
  let count = 0;
  let subtotal = 0;
  for (const item of cart.values()) {
    count += item.qty;
    subtotal += item.qty * item.price;
  }
  document.querySelectorAll("[data-cart-count]").forEach((badge) => (badge.textContent = count));
  document.querySelector("[data-open-cart]")?.setAttribute("aria-label", `Open cart, ${count} items`);

  // 3. The drawer: item list, empty message and the bill.
  const list = document.querySelector("[data-cart-items]");
  if (!list) return;
  list.replaceChildren(
    ...[...cart.values()].map((item) => {
      const li = document.createElement("li");
      li.innerHTML = `<span></span><span>× ${item.qty}</span><strong>${formatPaise(item.qty * item.price)}</strong>`;
      li.firstElementChild.textContent = item.name; // textContent, never innerHTML, for data
      return li;
    }),
  );
  document.querySelector("[data-cart-empty]").hidden = count > 0;

  const delivery = subtotal === 0 || subtotal >= FREE_DELIVERY_FROM ? 0 : DELIVERY_FEE;
  document.querySelector("[data-subtotal]").textContent = formatPaise(subtotal);
  document.querySelector("[data-delivery]").textContent = delivery ? formatPaise(delivery) : "FREE";
  document.querySelector("[data-total]").textContent = formatPaise(subtotal + delivery);
}
Code What it does document.querySelectorAll(".product-card").forEach(…) For every card on the page… card.querySelector("[data-add]").hidden = qty > 0; …hide ADD if it's in the cart… card.querySelector(".qty").hidden = qty === 0; …and show the stepper instead. card.querySelector("output").textContent = qty; …and write the number. for (const item of cart.values()) Loop over every cart item to add up the count and the subtotal. badge.textContent = count Update the red badge(s) in the header. setAttribute("aria-label", `Open cart, ${count} items`) Keep the cart button's spoken name in sync. the rest Draws the cart drawer.
