Explained in lesson 6.

docs.text:
1. Add a ninth product (Avocado 🥑, ₹149, fruits) by copying one <article>. Change every data-* value and both aria-labels.
  2. Add an "Out of stock" state: a data-out-of-stock attribute, a grey card, and a disabled ADD button (disabled attribute).
  3. Change the grid to show 3 cards per row on a phone. Which number in minmax() do you change?

docs.title: Solutions
docs.text:
Try each exercise yourself first, then open its solution to compare.

Every code solution below is applied in store-solved.html: the full store with all the exercises from every lesson done, tested in a real browser like the original. Its files are generated from store.html and store.js, so the snippets here are exactly what runs there.

1. A ninth product: avocado 
<article class="product-card" data-id="avocado" data-name="Hass Avocado" data-price="14900" data-category="fruits">
  <div class="product-media" role="img" aria-label="An avocado">🥑</div>
  <p class="product-eta">⏱ 10 MINS</p>
  <h3 class="product-title">Hass Avocado</h3>
  <p class="product-size">1 pc</p>
  <div class="product-footer">
    <p class="price"><strong>₹149</strong></p>
    <button class="btn btn--outline add-btn" type="button" data-add>ADD</button>
    <div class="qty" hidden>
      <button type="button" data-dec aria-label="Remove one Hass Avocado">−</button>
      <output aria-live="polite">0</output>
      <button type="button" data-inc aria-label="Add one more Hass Avocado">+</button>
    </div>
  </div>
</article>

Change every product-specific value: data-id (must be unique, it's the cart key), data-name, data-price in paise (₹149 = 14900), data-category, the emoji's aria-label, the title, the size, the price text and both stepper aria-labels. No CSS or JavaScript changes: the grid makes room, and the event delegation on the grid handles the new buttons.

2. An “Out of stock” state 
<article class="product-card" data-id="mango" data-name="Alphonso Mango" data-price="39900" data-category="fruits" data-out-of-stock>
  <div class="product-media" role="img" aria-label="Mangoes">🥭</div>
  <p class="product-eta">Back tomorrow</p>
  <h3 class="product-title">Alphonso Mango</h3>
  <p class="product-size">1 kg</p>
  <div class="product-footer">
    <p class="price"><strong>₹399</strong></p>
    <button class="btn btn--outline add-btn" type="button" data-add disabled>Sold out</button>
    <div class="qty" hidden>
      <button type="button" data-dec aria-label="Remove one Alphonso Mango">−</button>
      <output aria-live="polite">0</output>
      <button type="button" data-inc aria-label="Add one more Alphonso Mango">+</button>
    </div>
  </div>
</article>

/* Lesson 4, exercise 2: out-of-stock card */
.product-card[data-out-of-stock] .product-media {
  filter: grayscale(1);
  opacity: 0.5;
}
.product-card[data-out-of-stock] .product-title,
.product-card[data-out-of-stock] .price {
  color: var(--muted);
}
.add-btn:disabled {
  padding-inline: var(--space-2);
  white-space: nowrap;
  border-color: var(--line);
  background: var(--page);
  color: var(--muted);
  cursor: not-allowed;
}
Code Why data-out-of-stock A data attribute is both a CSS hook ([data-out-of-stock]) and something JavaScript can read. disabled on the button A disabled button can't be clicked or focused, and screen readers announce it as "dimmed"/"unavailable". No JavaScript needed. filter: grayscale(1); opacity: 0.5; A grey, faded picture says "unavailable" at a glance. .add-btn:disabled Style the disabled state so it doesn't look like a normal ADD button. "Back tomorrow" instead of "10 MINS" Tell people when it's coming back, not just that it's gone. 3. Three cards per row on a phone

Change the minimum in minmax(). A 375 px phone's container is 343 px wide; with two 12 px gaps, three cards get (343 − 24) / 3 ≈ 106 px each, so the minimum must be 106 px or less:

.product-grid {
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(100px, 100%), 1fr));
}

Now look at the cards: each has about 82 px of room inside its padding, and the price plus a 72 px ADD button no longer fit side by side, so they overflow. A layout change ripples into the components inside it. If you really want three columns, stack the footer as well (.product-footer { flex-direction: column; align-items: stretch; }). Most grocery apps keep two columns on phones for exactly this reason, which is why the solved store doesn't apply this one.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Storing prices as 189.00 and adding them with floats. Use whole paise.
  • Fixed card heights (height: 320px) to line up buttons. Text overflows as soon as a name is long or the user zooms. Use margin-top: auto.
  • A <div> with a click handler as the ADD button: no keyboard, no focus, no role.
  • One click listener per button: slow with hundreds of products and broken for cards added later. Use delegation.
  • Forgetting width/height on product images, so the grid jumps while images load.

docs.title: 5. Listing Page: Filters, Sort & Layout
docs.text:
Intermediate

A listing page (also called a category page or PLP, product listing page) shows many products with filters on the side and a toolbar (result count + sort) above the grid. On a phone the sidebar collapses into a "Filters" button.

docs.title: The page layout
docs.text:
The full section is long because it holds eight product cards, so here is its outline (the real code is in store.html):

<section class="section" id="shop" aria-labelledby="shop-title">
  <div class="section-head">
    <h2 id="shop-title">Daily essentials</h2>     <!-- section heading from lesson 3 -->
  </div>

  <div class="listing">                          <!-- the 2-column grid -->
    <details class="filters" data-filters>…</details>   <!-- column 1: sidebar -->

    <div>                                        <!-- column 2: one wrapper for toolbar + grid -->
      <div class="toolbar">…</div>
      <div class="product-grid" data-product-grid>
        <article class="product-card">…</article>      <!-- × 8, from lesson 4 -->
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
Code What it does id="shop" The target of the hero's "Shop now" link. <div class="listing"> The grid container. It has exactly two children, so it becomes exactly two columns. the second <div> Without this wrapper, the toolbar and the product grid would become two separate grid cells and land in the wrong places. Wrapping them keeps them together in column 2. 
.listing {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr;
  gap: var(--space-4);
  align-items: start;
}
@media (width >= 900px) {
  .listing {
    grid-template-columns: 240px 1fr;
  }
}
Code What it does .listing { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr; } Phone: one column. Filters on top, products below. gap: var(--space-4); 16 px between sidebar and products. align-items: start; Without it, grid stretches the sidebar to the full height of the product column. start keeps it its natural height (needed for sticky below). @media (width >= 900px) → grid-template-columns: 240px 1fr; Desktop: a fixed 240 px sidebar and the products in all the remaining space. We use 900 px here (not 768 px) because a sidebar + 2 product columns needs the room.

docs.title: ⑩ Filters: <details> + <fieldset>
docs.text:
<details class="filters" data-filters>
  <summary>Filters</summary>
  <fieldset>
    <legend>Category</legend>
    <label><input type="checkbox" name="category" value="fruits"> Fruits</label>
    <label><input type="checkbox" name="category" value="vegetables"> Vegetables</label>
    <label><input type="checkbox" name="category" value="dairy"> Dairy & Eggs</label>
    <label><input type="checkbox" name="category" value="bakery"> Bakery</label>
  </fieldset>
  <fieldset>
    <legend>Offers</legend>
    <label><input type="checkbox" name="deals" value="yes"> Only discounted items</label>
  </fieldset>
</details>
Code What it does <details class="filters" data-filters> A built-in disclosure: a box that opens and closes when you click its <summary>. Works with keyboard and screen readers, no JavaScript needed. <summary>Filters</summary> The always-visible clickable heading, with a ▸ / ▾ marker. <fieldset> Groups related form controls. <legend>Category</legend> The fieldset's title. Screen readers say "Category, group" before reading the checkboxes, so "Fruits" is heard in context. <label><input type="checkbox" name="category" value="fruits"> Fruits</label> Wrapping the input inside the label connects them without for/id, and makes the text clickable too (a bigger target). value is what JavaScript reads. name="deals" value="yes" A separate checkbox for "only discounted items".

}

}

@media (width >= 900px) {

Code What it does .filters { border; border-radius; background } Makes the filter panel a white card. summary { padding; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; } A bold, clickable header. .filters[open] summary { border-bottom: … } The open attribute is present while the details is expanded; only then draw a line under the summary. fieldset { margin: 0; border: 0; padding: … } Removes the browser's default grooved border and indent. legend { text-transform: uppercase; font-size: 0.8rem; color: var(--muted); } Small, grey, uppercase group titles. label { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: … } Checkbox and text in a centred row. input { accent-color: var(--brand); width: 18px; height: 18px; } accent-color recolours native checkboxes and radios with one line, no custom checkbox hacks. @media (width >= 900px) → position: sticky; top: 96px; On desktop the sidebar stays in view while you scroll the products. 96 px leaves room for the sticky header.

docs.title: The JavaScript: filter, sort, and open the sidebar on desktop
docs.text:
const filters = document.querySelector("[data-filters]");
const sortSelect = document.querySelector("[data-sort]");
const resultCount = document.querySelector("[data-result-count]");

function applyFilters() {
  const checked = [...filters.querySelectorAll("input[name=category]:checked")].map((input) => input.value);
  const dealsOnly = filters.querySelector("input[name=deals]").checked;
  let shown = 0;

  grid.querySelectorAll(".product-card").forEach((card) => {
    const categoryOk = checked.length === 0 || checked.includes(card.dataset.category);
    const dealOk = !dealsOnly || card.hasAttribute("data-deal");
    card.hidden = !(categoryOk && dealOk);
    if (!card.hidden) shown++;
  });
  resultCount.textContent = shown;
}

function applySort() {
  const cards = [...grid.querySelectorAll(".product-card")];
  const price = (card) => Number(card.dataset.price);
  if (sortSelect.value === "price-asc") cards.sort((a, b) => price(a) - price(b));
  if (sortSelect.value === "price-desc") cards.sort((a, b) => price(b) - price(a));
  if (sortSelect.value === "relevance") cards.sort((a, b) => a.dataset.order - b.dataset.order);
  grid.append(...cards); // append() moves existing elements, it doesn't copy them
}

if (filters && grid) {
  grid.querySelectorAll(".product-card").forEach((card, i) => (card.dataset.order = i));
  filters.addEventListener("change", applyFilters);
  sortSelect.addEventListener("change", applySort);

  // Filters are a collapsed <details> on phones and an always-open sidebar on desktop.
  const desktop = window.matchMedia("(width >= 900px)");
  const sync = () => (filters.open = desktop.matches);
  sync();
  desktop.addEventListener("change", sync);
}
Code What it does const filters = document.querySelector("[data-filters]"); Grab the three elements we need once, at the start. function applyFilters() Runs every time a checkbox changes. [...filters.querySelectorAll("input[name=category]:checked")] Every ticked category checkbox. [...] turns the NodeList into an array so we can use .map(). .map((input) => input.value) → e.g. ["fruits", "dairy"]. const dealsOnly = …checked; true if "Only discounted items" is ticked. const categoryOk = checked.length === 0 || checked.includes(card.dataset.category); Nothing ticked means "show all categories"; otherwise the card's category must be in the list. const dealOk = !dealsOnly || card.hasAttribute("data-deal"); If deals-only is on, the card must have data-deal. card.hidden = !(categoryOk && dealOk); Hide cards that fail either test. The grid closes the gaps automatically. resultCount.textContent = shown; Update "Showing N products" (and the live region announces it). function applySort() Runs when the sort dropdown changes. const cards = [...grid.querySelectorAll(".product-card")]; All cards as an array. cards.sort((a, b) => price(a) - price(b)); Sort by price, low to high. A negative result puts a first. Swap a and b for high to low. cards.sort((a, b) => a.dataset.order - b.dataset.order); "Relevance" = the original order, which we saved in data-order at start-up. grid.append(...cards); append() moves each existing card to the end, in the new order. Nothing is re-created, so each card keeps its state (quantity, focus). if (filters && grid) { … } Only wire this up on pages that have filters (the product-card demo doesn't). card.dataset.order = i Remember each card's original position for "Relevance". filters.addEventListener("change", applyFilters); One listener on the <details> catches changes from every checkbox inside it (delegation again). window.matchMedia("(width >= 900px)") The same media query as the CSS, in JavaScript. filters.open = desktop.matches; On desktop open the <details> so the sidebar is fully visible; on phones keep it closed. desktop.addEventListener("change", sync); Re-run when the window is resized across 900 px or a tablet is rotated.

Senior note: filters belong in the URL

In a real store, filters and sort are written to the URL (?category=dairy&sort=price-asc) with history.replaceState() and usually fetched from the server. Then a filtered page can be shared, bookmarked, and survives a refresh. Read the starting state with new URLSearchParams(location.search).

docs.text:
1. Add a Price fieldset with radio buttons ("Under ₹50", "₹50–₹100", "Over ₹100") and extend applyFilters().
  2. Add a "Clear all" button that unticks every checkbox and calls applyFilters().

docs.title: Solutions
docs.text:
Try each exercise yourself first, then open its solution to compare.

Every code solution below is applied in store-solved.html: the full store with all the exercises from every lesson done, tested in a real browser like the original. Its files are generated from store.html and store.js, so the snippets here are exactly what runs there.

1. A Price filter

The HTML: a radio group (only one choice at a time), with "Any price" ticked by default:

<fieldset>
  <legend>Price</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="price" value="any" checked> Any price</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="price" value="under-50"> Under ₹50</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="price" value="50-100"> ₹50 – ₹100</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="price" value="over-100"> Over ₹100</label>
</fieldset>

In applyFilters(), read which radio is ticked…

const range = filters.querySelector("input[name=price]:checked").value;

…test every card against it…

const priceOk = inPriceRange(Number(card.dataset.price), range);
card.hidden = !(categoryOk && dealOk && priceOk);

…using a small pure function (easy to read, easy to test):

function inPriceRange(paise, range) {
  if (range === "under-50") return paise < 5000;
  if (range === "50-100") return paise >= 5000 && paise <= 10000;
  if (range === "over-100") return paise > 10000;
  return true;   // "any"
}

Radios with the same name form a group, so ticking one unticks the others. The existing change listener on the <details> already hears them, so nothing else needs wiring.

2. A “Clear all” button 
<button class="btn btn--outline clear-filters" type="button" data-clear-filters>Clear all</button>

filters.querySelector("[data-clear-filters]").addEventListener("click", () => {
  for (const input of filters.querySelectorAll("input")) {
    input.checked = input.value === "any";   // untick everything except the "Any price" radio
  }
  applyFilters();   // setting .checked from code fires no "change" event, so filter by hand
});
applyFilters();     // also run once at the start, so the count is right from the first paint

The important line is the comment: setting .checked from JavaScript does not fire a change event, so the filter listener never hears about it. Call applyFilters() yourself. The extra applyFilters() at start-up makes "Showing 10 products" correct from the first paint, instead of a number typed into the HTML.

3. “No products match these filters” 
<p class="no-results" data-no-results hidden>No products match these filters.</p>

At the end of applyFilters():

document.querySelector("[data-no-results]").hidden = shown > 0;

/* Lesson 5, exercises 2 and 3: "Clear all" button and the empty message */
.filters .clear-filters {
  margin: 0 var(--space-4) var(--space-4);
}
.no-results {
  margin: 0;
  padding: var(--space-8) var(--space-4);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  background: var(--surface);
  color: var(--muted);
  text-align: center;
}

An empty result should never be a blank space. Say what happened and, ideally, offer the way out (the "Clear all" button).

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Building the filters toggle with a <div> and JavaScript. <details> is accessible and works with no JS at all.
  • Removing cards from the DOM to filter and re-creating them later: you lose quantities and focus. Toggle hidden.
  • A sidebar with a fixed height and its own scrollbar inside a scrolling page (two scrollbars). Use position: sticky.
  • Different breakpoints in CSS and JS (900 px in one, 1024 px in the other). Keep them identical.

docs.title: 6. Cart Drawer
docs.text:
Intermediate

The cart drawer slides in from the right when you tap the cart button. It lists what you've added, shows the bill (items total, delivery fee, amount to pay) and a checkout button. It is built on the native <dialog> element, which gives us focus trapping, the Esc key and a dark backdrop for free.

docs.title: What you see
docs.text:
Add a few products, then click Cart in the header. Close it with ×, Esc, or a click on the dark area. Open it full-size: 06-cart.html.

flowchart LR A["Click ADD / + / −"] --> B["setQty(card, qty)"] B --> C["cart Map updated"] C --> D["render()"] D --> E["Card: ADD or − n +"] D --> F["Header badge: 3"] D --> G["Drawer: items + bill"] H["Click Cart button"] --> I["drawer.showModal()"]

The key idea: state → render. Clicks never edit the screen directly. They change the cart Map, and render() redraws everything from it. The badge, the cards and the drawer can never disagree.

docs.title: The HTML
docs.text:
<dialog class="cart-drawer" id="cart" aria-labelledby="cart-title">
  <div class="cart-head">
    <h2 id="cart-title">My cart</h2>
    <form method="dialog">
      <button class="close-btn" aria-label="Close cart">×</button>
    </form>
  </div>
  <div class="cart-body">
    <p class="cart-empty" data-cart-empty>Your cart is empty. Add something fresh!</p>
    <ul class="cart-items" data-cart-items></ul>
  </div>
  <div class="cart-foot">
    <dl>
      <dt>Items total</dt>  <dd data-subtotal>₹0</dd>
      <dt>Delivery fee</dt> <dd data-delivery>₹0</dd>
      <dt class="total">To pay</dt> <dd class="total" data-total>₹0</dd>
    </dl>
    <button class="btn" type="button">Proceed to checkout</button>
  </div>
</dialog>
Code What it does <dialog class="cart-drawer" id="cart" aria-labelledby="cart-title"> A native dialog, hidden until opened. aria-labelledby gives it the name "My cart". <div class="cart-head"> Top bar: title + close button. <h2 id="cart-title">My cart</h2> The dialog's heading and accessible name. <form method="dialog"> A form that closes the dialog. Submitting it (clicking any button inside) closes the <dialog>, no JavaScript needed. <button class="close-btn" aria-label="Close cart">×</button> The × symbol needs a real label for screen readers. <div class="cart-body"> The scrolling middle part. <p class="cart-empty" data-cart-empty> Shown only when the cart is empty. Always design the empty state. <ul class="cart-items" data-cart-items></ul> Empty in HTML; JavaScript fills it with one <li> per product. <div class="cart-foot"> The bill, pinned to the bottom. <dl> with <dt> / <dd> A description list: name/value pairs. The right element for "Items total → ₹446". <dd data-subtotal> etc. JavaScript writes the amounts here. <button class="btn" type="button">Proceed to checkout</button> The final call to action. In a real store this goes to the checkout page.

docs.title: The CSS: turning a dialog into a drawer
docs.text:
.cart-drawer {
  width: min(400px, 100%);
  max-width: none;
  height: 100dvh;
  max-height: none;
  margin: 0 0 0 auto;
  padding: 0;
  border: 0;
  background: var(--page);
}
.cart-drawer[open] {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  animation: slide-in 0.2s ease-out;
}
.cart-drawer::backdrop {
  background: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5);
}
@keyframes slide-in {
  from { transform: translateX(100%); }
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .cart-drawer[open] {
    animation: none;
  }
}
Code What it does width: min(400px, 100%); 400 px wide on desktop, full width on a phone. max-width: none; max-height: none; Dialogs have a built-in maximum size with a margin around them; remove it. height: 100dvh; Full height of the screen. dvh (dynamic viewport height) accounts for the phone's address bar showing and hiding; 100vh would be too tall on mobile. margin: 0 0 0 auto; Dialogs are centred by default (margin: auto). Zero on top, right and bottom, auto on the left, pushes it to the right edge. padding: 0; border: 0; Removes the default dialog padding and border. .cart-drawer[open] { display: flex; flex-direction: column; } Only when open: stack head, body and foot vertically. (Don't set display on a closed dialog, or it would always show.) animation: slide-in 0.2s ease-out; Plays the slide-in animation when it opens. ::backdrop { background: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5); } The dark see-through layer behind a modal dialog, covering the page. @keyframes slide-in { from { transform: translateX(100%); } } Starts one full drawer-width to the right (off-screen) and animates to its normal position. Leaving out to means "to the normal style". @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) Some people get motion sickness and turn on "reduce motion" in their phone or OS settings. We respect it: no animation. 
.cart-head {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between;
  padding: var(--space-4);
  background: var(--surface);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line);
}
.cart-head h2 {
  margin: 0;
  font-size: 1.2rem;
}
.close-btn {
  border: 0;
  background: none;
  font-size: 1.5rem;
  line-height: 1;
  cursor: pointer;
}

.cart-body {
  flex: 1;
  overflow-y: auto;
  padding: var(--space-4);
}
.cart-items {
  display: grid;
  gap: var(--space-2);
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  list-style: none;
}
.cart-items li {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr auto auto;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--space-3);
  padding: var(--space-3);
  border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
  background: var(--surface);
}
.cart-empty {
  text-align: center;
  color: var(--muted);
}

.cart-foot {
  padding: var(--space-4);
  background: var(--surface);
  border-top: 1px solid var(--line);
}
.cart-foot dl {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr auto;
  gap: var(--space-1) var(--space-4);
  margin: 0 0 var(--space-4);
}
.cart-foot dd {
  margin: 0;
  text-align: right;
}
.cart-foot .total {
  font-weight: 700;
  font-size: 1.1rem;
}
.cart-foot .btn {
  width: 100%;
  padding-block: var(--space-3);
}
Code What it does .cart-head { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; } Title left, × right. .close-btn { border: 0; background: none; font-size: 1.5rem; } A plain big ×. .cart-body { flex: 1; overflow-y: auto; } The sticky-footer trick. flex: 1 makes the body take all the height left between head and foot; overflow-y: auto scrolls the items if there are many, while the bill stays visible. .cart-items { display: grid; gap: … } Items stacked with 8 px gaps. .cart-items li { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr auto auto; } Each item row: name (all spare space), "× 2", price. .cart-foot dl { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr auto; } Turns the description list into a two-column bill: labels left, amounts right. Each dt/dd pair fills one row automatically. .cart-foot dd { margin: 0; text-align: right; } Removes the default dd indent and right-aligns the money. .cart-foot .btn { width: 100%; } A full-width checkout button: the easiest thing to tap.

docs.title: Money: always whole paise
docs.text:
// Prices are stored in paise (1 rupee = 100 paise) as whole numbers.
// Whole numbers never suffer floating-point errors such as 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004.
const rupees = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-IN", {
  style: "currency",
  currency: "INR",
  maximumFractionDigits: 0,
});
const formatPaise = (paise) => rupees.format(paise / 100);

const FREE_DELIVERY_FROM = 19900; // ₹199
const DELIVERY_FEE = 2500;        // ₹25
Code What it does new Intl.NumberFormat("en-IN", { style: "currency", currency: "INR", maximumFractionDigits: 0 }) The browser's built-in formatter. Gives ₹1,23,456 with Indian digit grouping. Change to "en-US" / "USD" for $1,234. const formatPaise = (paise) => rupees.format(paise / 100); Store and add in paise; divide by 100 only to display. FREE_DELIVERY_FROM = 19900 ₹199, the free-delivery threshold from the announcement bar. Named constants beat magic numbers. DELIVERY_FEE = 2500 ₹25 when the order is below the threshold.

docs.title: Rendering the drawer (the end of render())
docs.text:
function render() {
  // 1. Each card shows "ADD" when it is not in the cart, and the − n + stepper when it is.
  document.querySelectorAll(".product-card").forEach((card) => {
    const qty = cart.get(card.dataset.id)?.qty ?? 0;
    card.querySelector("[data-add]").hidden = qty > 0;
    card.querySelector(".qty").hidden = qty === 0;
    card.querySelector("output").textContent = qty;
  });

  // 2. The red badge on the cart button.
  let count = 0;
  let subtotal = 0;
  for (const item of cart.values()) {
    count += item.qty;
    subtotal += item.qty * item.price;
  }
  document.querySelectorAll("[data-cart-count]").forEach((badge) => (badge.textContent = count));
  document.querySelector("[data-open-cart]")?.setAttribute("aria-label", `Open cart, ${count} items`);

  // 3. The drawer: item list, empty message and the bill.
  const list = document.querySelector("[data-cart-items]");
  if (!list) return;
  list.replaceChildren(
    ...[...cart.values()].map((item) => {
      const li = document.createElement("li");
      li.innerHTML = `<span></span><span>× ${item.qty}</span><strong>${formatPaise(item.qty * item.price)}</strong>`;
      li.firstElementChild.textContent = item.name; // textContent, never innerHTML, for data
      return li;
    }),
  );
  document.querySelector("[data-cart-empty]").hidden = count > 0;

  const delivery = subtotal === 0 || subtotal >= FREE_DELIVERY_FROM ? 0 : DELIVERY_FEE;
  document.querySelector("[data-subtotal]").textContent = formatPaise(subtotal);
  document.querySelector("[data-delivery]").textContent = delivery ? formatPaise(delivery) : "FREE";
  document.querySelector("[data-total]").textContent = formatPaise(subtotal + delivery);
}
Code What it does subtotal += item.qty * item.price; Whole-number maths only: exact. if (!list) return; Pages without a drawer (the product-card demo) stop here. list.replaceChildren(...items) Removes all old <li>s and inserts the new ones in one step. [...cart.values()].map((item) => { … }) One <li> per cart item. li.innerHTML = `<span></span>…` Builds the row's structure from a template with only our own markup and numbers in it. li.firstElementChild.textContent = item.name; The product name goes in with textContent, which never runs HTML. If a name ever contained <img onerror=…>, innerHTML would execute it (XSS); textContent just shows the text. document.querySelector("[data-cart-empty]").hidden = count > 0; Show the empty message only when there's nothing in the cart. const delivery = subtotal === 0 || subtotal >= FREE_DELIVERY_FROM ? 0 : DELIVERY_FEE; No fee for an empty cart or orders of ₹199 or more; otherwise ₹25. delivery ? formatPaise(delivery) : "FREE" Show the word "FREE" instead of "₹0": small copy details sell. formatPaise(subtotal + delivery) The amount to pay.

docs.title: Opening and closing
docs.text:
const drawer = document.querySelector("#cart");

document.querySelectorAll("[data-open-cart]").forEach((opener) =>
  opener.addEventListener("click", (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();  // the bottom-nav opener is a link; don't jump to "#"
    drawer?.showModal();     // modal: traps focus, Esc closes it, page behind is inert
  }),
);

// Clicking the dark backdrop closes the drawer (the click lands on <dialog> itself).
drawer?.addEventListener("click", (event) => {
  if (event.target === drawer) drawer.close();
});
Code What it does document.querySelectorAll("[data-open-cart]") Both the header cart button and the bottom-nav Cart link open the drawer. A data attribute lets any element do it. event.preventDefault(); The bottom-nav opener is a link to #; this stops it jumping to the top of the page. drawer?.showModal(); Opens the dialog as modal: focus moves inside it, Tab stays inside it, Esc closes it, the page behind can't be clicked, and focus returns to the cart button when it closes. Writing all that by hand takes ~100 lines. if (event.target === drawer) drawer.close(); Clicks on the drawer's contents have a child element as target. A click on the backdrop is reported on the <dialog> itself, so that's when we close.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
1. Add a "Remove" (🗑) button to each cart row that sets the quantity to 0.
  2. Show "Add ₹X more for free delivery" in the cart footer when the subtotal is below ₹199.
  3. Save the cart in localStorage so it survives a page refresh (JSON.stringify([...cart]) to save, new Map(JSON.parse(…)) to load).

docs.title: Solutions
docs.text:
Try each exercise yourself first, then open its solution to compare.

Every code solution below is applied in store-solved.html: the full store with all the exercises from every lesson done, tested in a real browser like the original. Its files are generated from store.html and store.js, so the snippets here are exactly what runs there.

1. A 🗑 Remove button in each cart row

Each row needs to know which product it is, so loop over the Map's [id, item] pairs instead of only its values:

...[...cart].map(([id, item]) => {
  const li = document.createElement("li");
  li.innerHTML = `<span></span><span>× ${item.qty}</span><strong>${formatPaise(item.qty * item.price)}</strong><button type="button" class="cart-remove">🗑</button>`;
  li.firstElementChild.textContent = item.name; // textContent, never innerHTML, for data
  const remove = li.querySelector(".cart-remove");
  remove.dataset.removeId = id;
  remove.setAttribute("aria-label", `Remove ${item.name} from cart`);
  return li;
}),

One listener on the list handles every 🗑 button, now and after every re-render:

// One listener on the cart list handles every 🗑 button (event delegation, like the product grid)
document.querySelector("[data-cart-items]")?.addEventListener("click", (event) => {
  const button = event.target.closest("[data-remove-id]");
  if (!button) return;
  const card = document.querySelector(`.product-card[data-id="${button.dataset.removeId}"]`);
  setQty(card, 0);   // quantity 0 = remove (lesson 4's setQty)
});

/* Lesson 6, exercises 1 and 2: a fourth column for the 🗑 button, and the free-delivery hint */
.cart-items li {
  grid-template-columns: 1fr auto auto auto;
}
.cart-remove {
  border: 0;
  background: none;
  font-size: 1rem;
  cursor: pointer;
}
.free-delivery-hint {
  margin: 0 0 var(--space-3);
  padding: var(--space-2) var(--space-3);
  border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
  background: var(--brand-soft);
  color: var(--brand-dark);
  font-size: 0.9rem;
  font-weight: 600;
}

Removing goes through the same setQty() as the product cards, so the card goes back to ADD, the badge updates and the bill is recalculated: one state, one render().

2. “Add ₹X more for free delivery” 
<p class="free-delivery-hint" data-free-hint hidden></p>

At the end of render():

const hint = document.querySelector("[data-free-hint]");
const missing = FREE_DELIVERY_FROM - subtotal;
hint.hidden = subtotal === 0 || missing <= 0;
hint.textContent = `Add ${formatPaise(missing)} more for free delivery`;

With ₹68 in the cart it reads "Add ₹131 more for free delivery"; at ₹199 or more, and for an empty cart, it disappears. Small nudges like this measurably raise the average order value in real stores.

3. Keep the cart after a refresh (localStorage)

Save at the end of every render() (every change goes through it):

try {
  localStorage.setItem("freshcart-cart", JSON.stringify([...cart]));   // Map → [[id, item], …] → text
} catch {
  // storage can be blocked (private mode, browser settings): the cart still works, it just isn't saved
}

Load once at start-up, before the first render():

try {
  const saved = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("freshcart-cart") ?? "[]");
  for (const [id, item] of saved) cart.set(id, item);
} catch {
  // nothing saved, storage blocked, or the saved text is broken: start with an empty cart
}
Code Why JSON.stringify([...cart]) A Map turns into {} with JSON.stringify; spread it into [[id, item], …] pairs first. localStorage.getItem(…) ?? "[]" The first visit has nothing saved (null), so start from an empty list. try / catch localStorage throws when storage is blocked (some private modes, strict settings) and JSON.parse throws on broken text. Either way the store must still work.

localStorage keeps strings only, per site, per browser, until the user clears it. A real store also saves the cart on the server, so it follows the user to their phone.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Building a modal from a <div> and forgetting focus trapping and Esc. Use <dialog> + showModal().
  • Using height: 100vh on mobile, so the bottom of the drawer (the checkout button!) hides under the browser's toolbar. Use 100dvh.
  • Updating the badge, the card and the drawer separately in each click handler. They drift apart. Keep one state and one render().
  • Putting product names into innerHTML: a cross-site scripting (XSS) hole as soon as names come from a server.

docs.title: 7. Footer & Mobile Bottom Nav
docs.text:
Beginner Intermediate

The footer holds everything people look for when they're stuck: company links, help, a newsletter signup and legal text. Shopping apps also add a bottom navigation bar on phones, because the bottom of the screen is where thumbs reach.

docs.title: What you see
docs.text: Open it full-size: 07-footer.html and make the window narrow: the footer columns stack and the bottom nav appears.

docs.title: ⑬ Footer: HTML
docs.text:

Code What it does <footer class="site-footer"> The contentinfo landmark: the site-wide footer. <div class="container"> Same width as the rest of the page. <div class="footer-grid"> The grid of four columns. <section> + <h2>FreshCart</h2> + <p> Column 1: about the store. <nav aria-label="Company"> Columns 2 and 3 are groups of links, so they're <nav> elements, each with a different label so screen readers can tell them apart. <h2> inside each column Column headings. Footer headings are usually h2: they are top-level sections of the page. <ul> + <li><a> Links as lists, as always. <form class="newsletter" action="#"> Column 4: email signup. <label class="visually-hidden" for="email"> The design has no visible label, but the input still needs one. <input id="email" type="email" … autocomplete="email" required> type="email" shows the @ keyboard on phones and checks the format. autocomplete="email" lets the browser fill it in. required blocks an empty submit. <div class="footer-bottom"> The bottom strip: copyright and payment methods.

docs.title: Footer: CSS
docs.text:
.site-footer {
  margin-top: var(--space-8);
  padding-top: var(--space-8);
  background: var(--text);
  color: #d5d9df;
  font-size: 0.9rem;

Code What it does margin-top: var(--space-8); padding-top: var(--space-8); Space above the footer, and inside it. background: var(--text); color: #d5d9df; Dark footer with light-grey text. A dark footer clearly says "the page ends here". grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(180px, 100%), 1fr)); Each column at least 180 px. Four columns on a desktop, two on a tablet, one on a phone, with no media queries. auto-fit (instead of auto-fill) stretches the columns to fill the row when there are fewer than fit. .site-footer h2 { font-size: 1rem; color: #fff; } Small white headings. The level is h2 for structure; the size is set by CSS. ul { margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; } Plain list. li + li { margin-top: var(--space-2); } The + (adjacent sibling) selector: "an li that comes right after another li". Adds space between items but not above the first. a:hover { text-decoration: underline; } Underline on hover so it's clear these are links.

Code What it does .newsletter { display: flex; gap: … } Input and button side by side. .newsletter input { flex: 1; min-width: 0; } The input takes the spare width and can shrink on narrow screens. background: #111418; color: #fff; border: 1px solid #4b5563; A dark input that fits the dark footer. .footer-bottom { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: space-between; } Copyright left, payments right; they wrap onto two lines on phones. border-top: 1px solid #3a404c; A subtle divider above the bottom strip.

  align-items: center;
  padding: var(--space-2) 0;
  font-size: 0.7rem;
  text-decoration: none;
}
.bottom-nav span {
  font-size: 1.25rem;
}
.bottom-nav a[aria-current="page"] {
  color: var(--brand);
  font-weight: 700;
}
body:has(.bottom-nav) {
  padding-bottom: 64px;
}
@media (width >= 768px) {
  .bottom-nav {
    display: none;
  }
  body:has(.bottom-nav) {
    padding-bottom: 0;
  }
}
Code What it does <nav class="bottom-nav" aria-label="Mobile"> A third navigation landmark, labelled. <a href="#" aria-current="page"> Home is the current page, so it's highlighted. <span aria-hidden="true">🏠</span>Home Icon above the word. The icon is decoration; the word is the link's name. Always keep a text label: icons alone are guessed wrong. <a href="#" data-open-cart> Opens the cart drawer (same hook as the header button, lesson 6). position: fixed; inset: auto 0 0 0; Fixed to the screen, not the page: it stays at the bottom while you scroll. inset is shorthand for top right bottom left: top: auto, and 0 from the right, bottom and left, so it spans the full width at the bottom. z-index: 10; Above the products. display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr); Four equal-width tabs. padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom); On iPhones without a home button, adds space so the tabs aren't hidden under the home-indicator bar. .bottom-nav a { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; } Icon above text, centred. a[aria-current="page"] { color: var(--brand); } Highlight the current tab, styled from the accessibility attribute. body:has(.bottom-nav) { padding-bottom: 64px; } :has() is the "parent selector": "the body, if it contains a bottom nav". The padding stops the fixed bar from covering the end of the footer. @media (width >= 768px) → display: none; and padding-bottom: 0 Desktops have the header links; no bottom bar needed.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
1. Add a fifth tab "Offers 🔥" (hint: change repeat(4, 1fr)).
  2. Add social links (Instagram, X, YouTube) to column 1 as a row of icons with aria-labels.
  3. Make the footer columns collapsible on phones with <details>, like the filters in lesson 5.

docs.title: Solutions
docs.text:
Try each exercise yourself first, then open its solution to compare.

Every code solution below is applied in store-solved.html: the full store with all the exercises from every lesson done, tested in a real browser like the original. Its files are generated from store.html and store.js, so the snippets here are exactly what runs there.

1. A fifth tab 
<a href="#"><span aria-hidden="true">🔥</span>Offers</a>

/* Lesson 7, exercise 1: five bottom-nav tabs */
.bottom-nav {
  grid-template-columns: repeat(5, 1fr);
}

repeat(5, 1fr) gives five equal columns. Five is the practical maximum for a bottom bar: at 375 px each tab is 75 px wide, about the smallest comfortable tap target with a label.

2. Social links 
<ul class="social" aria-label="Follow us">
  <li><a href="#" aria-label="FreshCart on Instagram">📸</a></li>
  <li><a href="#" aria-label="FreshCart on X">✖️</a></li>
  <li><a href="#" aria-label="FreshCart on YouTube">▶️</a></li>
</ul>

/* Lesson 7, exercise 2: round social icons in a row */
.site-footer .social {
  display: flex;
  gap: var(--space-2);
  margin-top: var(--space-4);   /* ".site-footer ul { margin: 0 }" is more specific than .social alone */
}
.site-footer .social li + li {
  margin-top: 0;
}
.social a {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  width: 40px;
  height: 40px;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: #2b3038;
  text-decoration: none;
}
.social a:hover {
  background: #3a404c;
}

Icon-only links must have an aria-label, or a screen reader announces "link, camera emoji". The list gets its own label ("Follow us") so it reads as a group. .site-footer .social is needed because the footer's .site-footer ul { margin: 0 } is more specific than .social alone.

3. Collapsible footer columns on phones

Wrap each link column in a <details>, with the heading inside the <summary>:

<nav aria-label="Company">
  <details class="footer-col" data-footer-col>
    <summary><h2>Company</h2></summary>
    <ul>
    <li><a href="#">About us</a></li>
    <li><a href="#">Careers</a></li>
      <li><a href="#">Blog</a></li>
    </ul>
  </details>
</nav>

Open them on desktop with the same matchMedia trick as the filters:

// Footer columns: collapsed <details> on phones, always open from 768 px (the same idea as the filters)
const footerColumns = document.querySelectorAll("[data-footer-col]");
const wide = window.matchMedia("(width >= 768px)");
const syncFooter = () => footerColumns.forEach((column) => (column.open = wide.matches));
syncFooter();
wide.addEventListener("change", syncFooter);

And replace the default ▸ marker with a +/− on the right:

/* Lesson 7, exercise 3: footer columns as <details> */
.footer-col summary {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: space-between;
  align-items: center;
  list-style: none;            /* hide the default ▸ marker… */
  cursor: pointer;
}
.footer-col summary::-webkit-details-marker {
  display: none;               /* …in Safari too */
}
.footer-col summary::after {
  content: "+";
  font-size: 1.25rem;
}
.footer-col[open] summary::after {
  content: "−";
}
@media (width >= 768px) {
  .footer-col summary {
    pointer-events: none;      /* always open on desktop: nothing to toggle */
  }
  .footer-col summary::after,
  .footer-col[open] summary::after {   /* list [open] too: it is more specific than the rule above */
    content: none;
  }
}

On a phone the footer shrinks to two tappable rows instead of six links; on desktop nothing changes. Without JavaScript the columns still work, they just start closed.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Icon-only bottom navs. Users don't know what 🗂️ means; add the word.
  • Forgetting the body padding, so the bottom nav covers the copyright line and the last product.
  • Using <div> for each link group instead of <nav> + a heading: screen-reader users lose their way.

docs.title: 8. Put It All Together
docs.text:
Beginner Intermediate Advanced

You've built every component. Now they go into one page, in the right order, with all the stylesheets and the script loaded.

docs.title: The finished page
docs.text: Open it full-size: store.html.

docs.title: Loading the files
docs.text:
<link rel="stylesheet" href="css/base.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="css/header.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="css/home.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="css/product.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="css/listing.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="css/cart.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="css/footer.css">
<script src="js/store.js" defer></script>
Code What it does base.css first Tokens and the reset must come before anything that uses them. one <link> per component Easy to find code: a header bug is in header.css. In production a build tool (Vite, Angular CLI) bundles them into one file. order: base → header → home → product → listing → cart → footer When two rules have equal specificity, the later one wins. Shared things first, specific things later. <script src="js/store.js" defer> defer downloads the script in parallel and runs it after the HTML is parsed, so querySelector finds every element. Without defer, a script in <head> runs before the body exists.

Component Tool Key line Header Grid areas grid-template-areas: "logo location search actions" Category nav, offers Flex / Grid + scroll overflow-x: auto; scroll-snap-type: x Hero Grid columns grid-template-columns: 1.4fr 1fr Category tiles, product grid, footer Grid auto-fill / auto-fit repeat(auto-fill, minmax(160px, 1fr)) Product card Flex column margin-top: auto on the footer Listing Grid columns grid-template-columns: 240px 1fr Cart badge Absolute positioning position: absolute; top: -8px; right: -8px Header, filters Sticky positioning position: sticky; top: 0 Bottom nav Fixed positioning position: fixed; inset: auto 0 0 0 Cart drawer <dialog> + flex column margin-left: auto; flex: 1 on the body

docs.title: Testing checklist
docs.text:
Do this for every page you build. It takes five minutes and finds most bugs.

  • 320 px wide (smallest phones): nothing scrolls sideways. In the DevTools console: document.documentElement.scrollWidth === innerWidth should be true.
  • 375 px, 768 px, 1024 px, 1440 px: every layout looks intended, not accidental.
  • Keyboard only: unplug the mouse. Tab reaches every link and button in a sensible order, the focus ring is always visible, Enter / Space work, Esc closes the cart.
  • Zoom to 200 %: text grows and nothing is cut off.
  • Screen reader (VoiceOver: Cmd+F5 on macOS; NVDA on Windows): headings list makes sense, buttons have names, the cart count is announced.
  • Lighthouse (DevTools → Lighthouse): Accessibility and Best Practices ≥ 95.
  • Slow network (DevTools → Network → Slow 4G): the page is usable before all images load, and nothing jumps around.
  • Reduce motion (DevTools → Rendering → Emulate prefers-reduced-motion): the drawer opens without sliding.

This page is tested automatically

The repository's coding-interview/run-tests.mjs opens store.html in a real Chromium browser on every pull request and checks: no sideways scroll at 320 px, the header layout at phone and desktop widths, ADD → stepper → cart badge → drawer totals (including the free-delivery rule), filters and sort, and that the drawer opens and closes with the keyboard.

13-ecommerce-store: 7 checks, 0 failures

  ✔ header: search on its own row on a phone, one row on desktop
  ✔ product grid: 2 cards per row at 375 px, 4 at 1280 px; ADD buttons line up
  ✔ ADD → stepper → badge → drawer totals (₹25 fee below ₹199, FREE above)
  ✔ cart drawer: modal, full width on a phone, Esc closes, empty state
  ✔ filters + sort: Dairy shows 3, deals-only narrows, price sort reorders
  ✔ phone: filters collapsed, bottom nav visible and opens the cart; hidden on desktop

docs.text:
Each one practises a skill real frontend jobs use every day.

# Exercise You practise 1 Add a dark mode by overriding the tokens inside @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { … } } Design tokens 2 Build a product detail page (product.html): image gallery, title, price, size selector (radio buttons), "Add to cart", description in <details> Reusing components, forms 3 Add search suggestions: as you type, show matching product names under the search box (debounce the input, see Coding Interview #9) Events, debounce 4 Load the products from a JSON file with fetch() and build the cards with a <template> element Data-driven UI 5 Show skeleton loaders (grey pulsing boxes) for 1 second before products appear Loading states, animation 6 Build a checkout page: address form with validation, delivery slot picker, order summary Forms, accessibility 7 Turn each component into an Angular component (<app-header>, <app-product-card>) or a Web Component (<product-card>) Component frameworks

docs.title: Where this fits in a real project
docs.text:
In a production store the same components appear, but:

  • the HTML comes from Angular/React components instead of one file, and each component owns its CSS;
  • products, prices and stock come from an API, and the cart lives on the server so it follows you across devices;
  • prices are still integers in the smallest currency unit, exactly like data-price="18900" here;
  • images go through a CDN with srcset sizes;
  • everything is tested in CI with real browsers, just like this page.

The layout skills don't change. Learn them once here with plain HTML and CSS, and every framework becomes easier.

docs.title: HTML5: How It Works
docs.text:
HTML (HyperText Markup Language) describes what content is: a heading, a paragraph, a button, a navigation menu. CSS then describes how it looks, and JavaScript describes how it behaves.

What “HTML5” means today

"HTML5" was the 2014 W3C snapshot. Since 2019 there's one HTML standard, the HTML Living Standard maintained by WHATWG, and it changes continuously. When people say HTML5 today, they mean "modern HTML". This playbook follows the Living Standard as of 2026.

docs.title: Elements, tags and attributes Beginner
docs.text:
<a href="https://example.com" target="_blank">Visit example</a>
Part In the example Meaning Opening tag <a …> Starts the element Attribute href="https://example.com" Extra information: name + value Content Visit example What's inside Closing tag </a> Ends the element Element the whole thing Opening tag + content + closing tag Visit example

Void elements have no content and no closing tag: <br>, <hr>, <img>, <input>, <meta>, <link>, <source>, <track>, <wbr>, <area>, <base>, <col>, <embed>. Writing <br/> with a slash is allowed but has no effect in HTML.

Boolean attributes are on when present and off when absent: <input disabled>. Writing disabled="false" still disables it.

docs.title: The DOM Beginner
docs.text:
The browser reads your HTML and builds a tree of objects called the DOM (Document Object Model). CSS styles the DOM and JavaScript changes it.

<body>
  <h1>Title</h1>
  <p>Hello <strong>world</strong></p>
</body>
flowchart TD body --> h1 --> t1["'Title'"] body --> p p --> t2["'Hello '"] p --> strong --> t3["'world'"]

docs.title: Block vs inline Beginner
docs.text:
By default, each element has a CSS display value.

  • Block elements (<div>, <p>, <h1>, <section>, <ul>) start on a new line and stretch to fill the width.
  • Inline elements (<span>, <a>, <strong>, <em>, <code>) sit inside a line of text and are only as wide as their content.
<div style="background:#ffd8c2">I'm a block div</div>
<div style="background:#c7e2ff">So am I, on a new line</div>
<span style="background:#ffd8c2">I'm inline</span>
<span style="background:#c7e2ff">I sit on the same line</span>
I'm a block div So am I, on a new line I'm inline I sit on the same line

Senior note · 🟡 Intermediate

"Block" and "inline" are CSS behaviours, not HTML rules. The HTML spec uses content categories instead: flow, phrasing, heading, sectioning, embedded, interactive, metadata. These decide what can be nested inside what. For example, <p> accepts only phrasing content, so <p><div>…</div></p> is invalid; the browser closes the <p> before the <div>.

docs.title: Content categories Intermediate
docs.text:
Category Examples What it means Metadata title, meta, link, style, script, base Describes the document; lives in <head> Flow almost everything in <body> Allowed wherever body content is allowed Sectioning article, aside, nav, section Defines a section with its own heading scope Heading h1–h6, hgroup Section titles Phrasing span, a, em, strong, img, input Text-level content inside paragraphs Embedded img, video, audio, iframe, svg, canvas Imports another resource Interactive a[href], button, input, select, details, label The user can interact with it

Rule of thumb: interactive content can't be nested inside interactive content. A <button> inside an <a> is invalid and confuses screen readers and keyboards.

docs.title: Semantic HTML: why it matters Beginner
docs.text:
<!-- ❌ Div soup -->
<div class="header"><div class="nav">…</div></div>
<div class="button" onclick="save()">Save</div>

<!-- ✅ Semantic -->
<header><nav>…</nav></header>
<button type="button" onclick="save()">Save</button>

The semantic version gives you, for free:

  • Keyboard support: <button> is focusable and responds to Enter and Space.
  • Screen reader support: announced as "Save, button"; landmarks let users jump to the nav.
  • SEO: search engines understand page structure.
  • Less code: no tabindex, role or key handlers to write and maintain.

docs.title: Validate your HTML Intermediate
docs.text:
• W3C Nu HTML Checker catches nesting errors and invalid attributes.
  • In CI, run html-validate or vnu-jar on built pages.
  • Browsers silently fix bad HTML, but each browser can fix it differently. Valid HTML gives a predictable DOM.

docs.title: The minimum valid page Beginner
docs.text:
Learn this skeleton by heart. Every page you build starts here.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>My first page</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Hello</h1>
</body>
</html>
Line Why it's there <!doctype html> Tells the browser to use standards mode. Without it you get "quirks mode", which emulates 1990s browser bugs. <html lang="en"> Root element. lang sets pronunciation for screen readers, hyphenation, spell-check and translation. <meta charset="utf-8"> Character encoding. Must be in the first 1024 bytes. Without it, characters like é or ₹ can turn into Ã©. <meta name="viewport" …> Makes mobile browsers use the device width instead of pretending to be 980px wide. Without it, responsive design doesn't work. <title> Shown in the browser tab, bookmarks and search results. Required.

docs.title: <!doctype html> Beginner
docs.text: Use: switches the browser into standards mode. Not an element, it's a declaration. Case-insensitive.

docs.title: <html> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: the root of the document. Everything else goes inside it.

Key attributes: lang (always set it), dir="rtl" for right-to-left languages such as Arabic and Hebrew.

docs.title: <head> Beginner
docs.text: Use: a container for metadata: things about the page, not shown in the page. Contains title, meta, link, style, script, base, noscript, template.

docs.title: <title> Beginner
docs.text:
<title>Pricing · Acme Cloud</title>

Use: the document's name. Put the specific part first ("Pricing") and the brand last, so tabs stay readable when they're narrow.

docs.title: <meta> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: metadata that has no dedicated element.

<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<meta name="description" content="Simple, predictable pricing for teams of any size.">
<meta name="theme-color" content="#e4572e">
<meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">
<meta name="robots" content="index, follow">

<!-- Open Graph: link previews in Slack, WhatsApp, LinkedIn, etc. -->
<meta property="og:title" content="Acme Cloud Pricing">
<meta property="og:description" content="Simple, predictable pricing.">
<meta property="og:image" content="https://acme.example/og.png">
<meta property="og:url" content="https://acme.example/pricing">
<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image">
name / property What it does viewport Mobile layout width. Never add user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1: they block zoom, which fails WCAG. description Snippet text in search results (~155 characters). theme-color Colours the browser UI on mobile. Accepts a media attribute for light/dark values. color-scheme Tells the browser your page supports dark mode, so form controls and scrollbars adapt before CSS loads. robots Search engine indexing rules. og:*, twitter:* Social preview cards.

Senior note · 🟠 Advanced

http-equiv meta tags act like HTTP headers (Content-Security-Policy, refresh). Prefer real HTTP headers: they apply before parsing and some directives (like CSP's frame-ancestors) are ignored in meta form.

docs.title: <link> Beginner → Advanced
docs.text:
Use: connects the page to external resources.

<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/main.css">
<link rel="icon" href="/favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">
<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/apple-touch-icon.png">
<link rel="manifest" href="/site.webmanifest">
<link rel="canonical" href="https://acme.example/pricing">

<!-- Performance hints -->
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link rel="preload" href="/fonts/inter.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>
<link rel="preload" href="/hero.avif" as="image" fetchpriority="high">
<link rel="modulepreload" href="/js/app.js">
<link rel="dns-prefetch" href="https://cdn.example.com">

<!-- Print-only stylesheet -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/print.css" media="print">
rel Use stylesheet Load CSS. Blocks rendering until loaded (that's on purpose). icon Favicon. SVG favicons can include a prefers-color-scheme media query. manifest Web app manifest for installable PWAs. canonical The preferred URL for duplicate content (SEO). preconnect Open a connection to another origin early. Use for 1–3 critical origins only. preload Fetch a resource you will need on this page, now, with high priority. modulepreload Preload a JS module and its parse. prefetch Fetch a resource the next page might need, at low priority. alternate Alternate versions: hreflang translations, RSS feeds.

docs.title: <style> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: CSS inside the HTML document.

<style>
  body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; }
</style>

Senior note · 🟠 Advanced

Inlining the critical CSS (what's needed for the first screen) in a <style> tag and loading the rest async can noticeably improve LCP. Don't inline everything; you lose browser caching across pages.

docs.title: <script> Beginner → Advanced
docs.text:
Use: runs JavaScript, or holds data (type="application/ld+json", type="importmap").

<!-- Classic script: blocks HTML parsing while it downloads and runs -->
<script src="legacy.js"></script>

<!-- defer: download in parallel, run in order after HTML is parsed -->
<script src="app.js" defer></script>

<!-- async: download in parallel, run as soon as it arrives (any order) -->
<script src="analytics.js" async></script>

<!-- module: deferred by default, strict mode, supports import/export -->
<script type="module" src="main.js"></script>

<!-- import map: name bare imports -->
<script type="importmap">
  { "imports": { "lit": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/lit@3/+esm" } }
</script>

<!-- Structured data for search engines -->
<script type="application/ld+json">
  { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "Organization", "name": "Acme" }
</script>
gantt dateFormat X axisFormat %s section Plain script Parse HTML :0, 3 Download :3, 5 Execute :5, 6 Parse rest :6, 9 section defer Parse HTML :0, 9 Download :1, 4 Execute :9, 10 section async Parse HTML :0, 4 Download :1, 4 Execute :4, 5 Parse rest :5, 9

Rule of thumb: use type="module" or defer for your app code. Use async only for independent scripts like analytics.

docs.title: <noscript> Intermediate
docs.text:
Use: content shown only when JavaScript is disabled.

<noscript>
  <p>This app needs JavaScript. Here's a <a href="/basic">basic version</a>.</p>
</noscript>

docs.title: <base> Advanced
docs.text:
Use: sets the base URL for every relative URL in the document. Only one per page.

<base href="https://docs.example.com/v2/">

Warning

<base> also changes where #anchor links point. <a href="#top"> becomes https://docs.example.com/v2/#top, which can break in-page navigation. Avoid it unless you need it.

docs.title: <body> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: contains everything visible on the page. One per document.

Senior note · 🔴 Expert

The browser builds the DOM top to bottom. Stylesheets in <head> block rendering; scripts without defer/async block parsing. A good <head> order: charset → viewport → title → preconnect → critical CSS → preload → stylesheets → deferred scripts → SEO and social meta. Tools like capo.js check this ordering for you.

docs.title: Forms & Inputs
docs.text: Forms are where most accessibility bugs live and where native HTML saves you the most code. Built-in elements give you keyboard support, mobile keyboards, validation and autofill for free.

docs.title: <form> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: collects user input and sends it to a server.

<form action="/signup" method="post">
  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input id="email" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" required>
  <button type="submit">Sign up</button>
</form>
Email Sign up Attribute Use action URL to send the data to (defaults to the current URL) method get (data in the URL; use for search/filter) or post (data in the body; use for changes) enctype multipart/form-data is required for file uploads novalidate Turn off built-in validation (you'll do it in JS) autocomplete on / off for the whole form

The name attribute on each control is what gets submitted. No name, no data.

docs.title: <label> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: the visible, clickable name of a control. Clicking the label focuses or toggles the input, which makes small checkboxes much easier to hit.

<!-- Explicit: for + id -->
<label for="name">Full name</label>
<input id="name" name="name">

<!-- Implicit: wrap the input -->
<label><input type="checkbox" name="terms"> I accept the terms</label>
Full name I accept the terms

Placeholder is not a label

Placeholder text disappears when the user types, is usually low-contrast, and isn't reliably announced. Every input needs a real <label>.

docs.title: <input>: all 22 types Beginner
docs.text: Each type gives a different control, a different mobile keyboard and different built-in validation. Try them in the Output boxes.

docs.title: Text-like inputs
docs.text:
<label>text     <input type="text" placeholder="Any text"></label>
<label>email    <input type="email" placeholder="you@example.com"></label>
<label>password <input type="password" value="secret123"></label>
<label>search   <input type="search" placeholder="Search…"></label>
<label>tel      <input type="tel" placeholder="+91 98765 43210"></label>
<label>url      <input type="url" placeholder="https://"></label>
<label>number   <input type="number" min="0" max="10" step="1" value="3"></label>
text email password search tel url number Type Mobile keyboard Built-in validation text Standard none email Has @ and . Must look like an email; multiple allows a comma list password Standard, masked none search "Search"/"Go" key; may show a clear ✕ none tel Phone keypad none (phone formats vary; use pattern) url Has / and .com Must be an absolute URL number Numeric min, max, step

Senior note · 🟠 Advanced

Don't use type="number" for things that are digits but not quantities (OTP codes, card numbers, PIN codes, ZIP codes). Spinners and scroll-wheel changes make no sense there, and leading zeros are lost. Use type="text" inputmode="numeric" autocomplete="one-time-code" instead.

docs.title: Date and time inputs
docs.text:
<input type="date">
<input type="time">
<input type="datetime-local">
<input type="month">
<input type="week">
date time datetime-local month week

The value is always submitted in ISO format (2026-10-19) regardless of how it's displayed. month and week aren't supported in Firefox/Safari desktop; they fall back to a text field.

docs.title: Choice inputs
docs.text:
<fieldset>
  <legend>Size</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="size" value="s"> Small</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="size" value="m" checked> Medium</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="size" value="l"> Large</label>
</fieldset>

<label><input type="checkbox" checked> Gift wrap</label>
<label><input type="checkbox" switch> Notifications</label>  <!-- Safari 17.4+ switch -->
Size Small Medium Large

Gift wrap Notifications

  • Radio: pick exactly one. All radios in a group share the same name. Arrow keys move between them.
  • Checkbox: on/off, independently. Can be set to indeterminate via JS (the "some selected" state).

docs.title: Other inputs
docs.text:
<input type="range" min="0" max="100" value="60">
<input type="color" value="#e4572e">
<input type="file" accept="image/*" multiple>
<input type="hidden" name="csrf" value="abc123">
<input type="image" src="go.png" alt="Go">
<input type="submit" value="Submit">
<input type="reset" value="Reset">
<input type="button" value="Plain button">
range color file hidden(nothing visible, still submitted) image submit / reset / button

<input type=submit> vs <button>

Prefer <button>: it can contain HTML (icons, <span>s), while <input> buttons only take a value string.

docs.title: All 22 types at a glance
docs.text: Type Level Type Level text 🟢 date 🟢 email 🟢 time 🟢 password 🟢 datetime-local 🟡 search 🟢 month 🟡 tel 🟢 week 🟡 url 🟢 color 🟡 number 🟢 file 🟡 checkbox 🟢 hidden 🟡 radio 🟢 image 🟠 range 🟡 submit 🟢 button 🟢 reset 🟢

docs.title: Validation attributes Beginner
docs.text:
<input required>
<input minlength="3" maxlength="20">
<input type="number" min="1" max="99" step="1">
<input pattern="[A-Z]{3}-[0-9]{4}" title="Format: ABC-1234">
Order code Check

Try submitting with an empty or wrongly formatted value: the browser shows its own error bubble.

Style validation state with CSS. :user-invalid only matches after the user has interacted, so fields don't show red before anyone types:

input:user-invalid { border-color: crimson; }
input:user-valid   { border-color: seagreen; }

docs.title: autocomplete, inputmode, enterkeyhint Intermediate
docs.text:
<input name="name"   autocomplete="name">
<input name="email"  autocomplete="email" type="email">
<input name="phone"  autocomplete="tel" type="tel">
<input name="addr"   autocomplete="street-address">
<input name="pin"    autocomplete="postal-code" inputmode="numeric">
<input name="cc"     autocomplete="cc-number" inputmode="numeric">
<input name="otp"    autocomplete="one-time-code" inputmode="numeric">
<input name="new-pw" autocomplete="new-password" type="password">
<input name="q"      enterkeyhint="search" type="search">
  • autocomplete tokens let browsers and password managers fill fields correctly. It's also a WCAG 2.2 requirement (1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose).
  • inputmode picks the on-screen keyboard: none, text, decimal, numeric, tel, search, email, url.
  • enterkeyhint changes the label on the mobile Enter key: enter, done, go, next, previous, search, send.

docs.title: <button> Beginner
docs.text:
<button type="submit">Submit (default in a form)</button>
<button type="button">Plain action</button>
<button type="reset">Reset form</button>
<button type="button" disabled>Disabled</button>
Submit (default in a form) Plain action Reset form Disabled

docs.title: <select>, <option>, <optgroup> Beginner
docs.text:
<label for="city">City</label>
<select id="city" name="city">
  <option value="">Choose a city</option>
  <optgroup label="India">
    <option value="blr" selected>Bengaluru</option>
    <option value="mum">Mumbai</option>
  </optgroup>
  <optgroup label="Germany">
    <option value="ber">Berlin</option>
    <option value="muc" disabled>Munich (soon)</option>
  </optgroup>
</select>

<label for="skills">Skills (multi-select)</label>
<select id="skills" name="skills" multiple size="4">
  <option>HTML</option><option>CSS</option><option>JS</option><option>A11y</option>
</select>
City Choose a city Bengaluru Mumbai Berlin Munich (soon) Skills HTMLCSSJSA11y

New: customizable <select> · 🟠 Advanced

Chromium 135+ supports fully styleable selects with select, ::picker(select) { appearance: base-select; }, including rich HTML inside <option>. Other browsers ignore it and show the normal select, so it's safe progressive enhancement.

docs.title: <datalist> Intermediate
docs.text:
Use: suggestions for a text input. Unlike <select>, users can still type anything.

<label for="browser">Browser</label>
<input id="browser" list="browsers">
<datalist id="browsers">
  <option value="Chrome"></option>
  <option value="Firefox"></option>
  <option value="Safari"></option>
  <option value="Edge"></option>
</datalist>
Browser

docs.title: <textarea> Beginner
docs.text:
<label for="msg">Message</label>
<textarea id="msg" name="msg" rows="4" cols="40" maxlength="500"></textarea>
Message

The demo uses field-sizing: content (Chromium 123+): the textarea grows as you type, with no JavaScript.

docs.title: <fieldset> and <legend> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: group related controls with a caption. Required for radio groups so screen readers announce the question ("Size, radio group"). <fieldset disabled> disables everything inside.

<fieldset>
  <legend>Shipping address</legend>
  <label>Street <input name="street"></label>
  <label>City <input name="city"></label>
</fieldset>
Shipping address Street City

docs.title: <output> Intermediate
docs.text:
Use: the result of a calculation or user action. Screen readers announce changes to it.

<form oninput="total.value = Number(a.value) * Number(b.value)">
  <input name="a" type="number" value="4"> ×
  <input name="b" type="number" value="5"> =
  <output name="total" for="a b">20</output>
</form>
× = 20

docs.title: <progress> and <meter> Beginner
docs.text:
• <progress>: how far a task has got. No value = indeterminate (spinning).
  • <meter>: a measurement within a known range (disk usage, password strength). Turns yellow/red past low/high.
<label>Upload <progress value="70" max="100">70%</progress></label>
<label>Loading <progress></progress></label>

<label>Disk <meter value="0.3" low="0.6" high="0.85" optimum="0.1">30%</meter></label>
<label>Disk <meter value="0.7" low="0.6" high="0.85" optimum="0.1">70%</meter></label>
<label>Disk <meter value="0.95" low="0.6" high="0.85" optimum="0.1">95%</meter></label>

Upload 70% Loading

Disk 30% Disk 70% Disk 95%

Senior note · 🔴 Expert

Form UX checklist for design reviews: one column; labels above inputs; mark optional fields rather than required ones when most are required; inline errors linked with aria-describedby; error summary at the top on submit, with focus moved to it; never clear user input on error; autocomplete on every personal-data field; minimum 24×24 CSS px targets (WCAG 2.5.8); don't disable the submit button (explain what's wrong instead).

docs.title: Global Attributes
docs.text: Global attributes work on every HTML element.

docs.title: Core Beginner
docs.text: Attribute Use Example id Unique identifier on the page. Targets for links (#id), labels (for), ARIA and JS. <section id="pricing"> class Space-separated names for CSS and JS. Reusable. <div class="card card--featured"> style Inline CSS. Highest specificity in author styles; avoid except for dynamic values. <div style="--progress: 40%"> title Advisory tooltip. Not accessible on touch or keyboard; don't rely on it. <abbr title="…"> lang Language of the content. <p lang="hi">नमस्ते</p> dir Text direction: ltr, rtl, auto. <p dir="auto"> hidden Hides the element (like display:none). <div hidden>

docs.title: hidden and hidden="until-found" Intermediate
docs.text:
<p hidden>You can't see me.</p>
<div hidden="until-found">Browser find-in-page (Ctrl+F) can reveal me.</div>

until-found (Chromium 102+; Firefox and Safari recently) keeps content findable and indexable while collapsed, which is perfect for accordions. The beforematch event fires before it's revealed.

docs.title: data-* custom data Beginner
docs.text:
<button data-product-id="4821" data-variant="blue">Add to cart</button>

<script>
  btn.dataset.productId;   // "4821" (kebab-case → camelCase)
</script>

<style>
  [data-variant="blue"] { background: royalblue; color: white; }
</style>
Add to cart

docs.title: Interaction Intermediate
docs.text:
Attribute Use tabindex="0" Make a non-focusable element focusable, in DOM order. tabindex="-1" Focusable by script (el.focus()) but not by Tab. Used for headings you move focus to. tabindex="1+" ❌ Never: it breaks the natural focus order. autofocus Focus on page load / dialog open. Use sparingly. accesskey Keyboard shortcut. Conflicts with assistive tech shortcuts, so rarely recommended. contenteditable Makes content editable: true, false, plaintext-only. draggable true to allow native drag and drop. spellcheck true / false inputmode, enterkeyhint Virtual keyboard hints (also work on contenteditable). autocapitalize off, sentences, words, characters 
<p contenteditable="true">Click and edit this text.</p>

Click and edit this text.

docs.title: inert Intermediate Baseline 2023
docs.text:
Use: makes an element and its whole subtree non-interactive: no focus, no clicks, hidden from assistive tech. Use it on the page behind an off-canvas menu or a custom modal.

<main inert>…</main>
<nav class="drawer open">…</nav>
I'm inert: try clicking or tabbing to me inert link

docs.title: popover Intermediate
docs.text: Turns any element into a popover. See Interactive → Popover API.

docs.title: Accessibility: role and aria-* Advanced
docs.text:
ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications) changes what assistive technology announces. It doesn't change behaviour: role="button" won't make a <div> keyboard-operable.

The five rules of ARIA:

  1. If a native HTML element does the job, use it instead of ARIA.
  2. Don't change native semantics (<h2 role="tab"> ❌) unless you really must.
  3. All interactive ARIA controls must be keyboard operable.
  4. Don't use role="presentation" or aria-hidden="true" on a focusable element.
  5. All interactive elements must have an accessible name.
Attribute Use aria-label Accessible name when there's no visible text: <button aria-label="Close">✕</button> aria-labelledby Name from another element's text (by id) aria-describedby Extra description: hint or error text aria-expanded true/false on a button that toggles something aria-controls id of the element the control affects aria-current page, step, date… marks the current item in a set aria-live polite / assertive: announce dynamic updates (toasts, results counts) aria-hidden="true" Hide decorative content from assistive tech aria-invalid Mark a field as invalid aria-busy Region is updating aria-pressed Toggle buttons (true / false / mixed) 
<button aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="filters">Filters</button>
<div id="filters" hidden>…</div>

<label for="pw">Password</label>
<input id="pw" type="password" aria-describedby="pw-hint pw-err" aria-invalid="true">
<p id="pw-hint">At least 12 characters.</p>
<p id="pw-err">Too short.</p>

<p aria-live="polite" id="status">3 results</p>

docs.title: Others Advanced
docs.text: Attribute Use translate="no" Don't machine-translate (brand names, code) nonce Allow this inline script/style under a Content Security Policy part Expose a shadow-DOM element for styling with ::part() slot Assign a child to a named <slot> in a web component is Customized built-in element (not supported in Safari) itemscope, itemtype, itemprop Microdata for structured data (JSON-LD is usually preferred) writingsuggestions false to turn off browser AI writing suggestions in a field

docs.title: Inline Text Semantics
docs.text: Elements that give meaning to words and phrases inside a paragraph.

docs.title: <a> Anchor (link) Beginner
docs.text:
Use: a hyperlink to another page, a file, a section of the same page, an email address or a phone number.

<p>
  <a href="/about">Internal link</a> ·
  <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org" target="_blank" rel="noopener">External, new tab</a> ·
  <a href="#forms">Jump to a section</a> ·
  <a href="mailto:hi@example.com">Email us</a> ·
  <a href="tel:+911234567890">Call us</a> ·
  <a href="/report.pdf" download>Download PDF</a>
</p>

Internal link · External, new tab · Jump to a section · Email us · Call us · Download PDF

Key attributes: href, target, rel (noopener, noreferrer, nofollow, sponsored, ugc), download, hreflang, referrerpolicy.

Link or button?

Links go somewhere (change the URL). Buttons do something (submit, open, toggle). Never use <a href="#" onclick="…"> for an action, and never put a <button> inside an <a>.

Senior note · 🟡 Intermediate

Modern browsers apply rel="noopener" to target="_blank" automatically, but writing it is still good practice for older browsers. Link text must make sense out of context: "Read the pricing guide", not "Click here".

docs.title: <strong> vs <b> Beginner
docs.text:
• <strong>: strong importance, seriousness or urgency.
  • <b>: draws attention without extra importance (keywords, product names).
<p><strong>Warning:</strong> this action can't be undone.</p>
<p>The <b>Pro</b> plan includes priority support.</p>

Warning: this action can't be undone.

The Pro plan includes priority support.

docs.title: <em> vs <i> Beginner
docs.text:
• <em>: stress emphasis that changes the meaning of the sentence.
  • <i>: alternate voice: foreign words, technical terms, thoughts, ship names.
<p>I <em>never</em> said she stole the money.</p>
<p>The word <i lang="fr">déjà vu</i> comes from French.</p>

I never said she stole the money.

The word déjà vu comes from French.

docs.title: <u>, <s>, <mark>, <small> Beginner
docs.text:
<p><u>Speling</u> errors are often underlined. (u = unarticulated annotation)</p>
<p><s>₹999</s> ₹699 (s = no longer accurate)</p>
<p>Search results for “grid”: CSS <mark>grid</mark> layout. (mark = highlighted/relevant)</p>
<p><small>Prices include GST. (small = side comments, fine print)</small></p>

Speling errors are often underlined. (u = unarticulated annotation)

₹999 ₹699 (s = no longer accurate)

Search results for “grid”: CSS grid layout. (mark = highlighted/relevant)

Prices include GST. (small = side comments, fine print)

docs.title: <sub> and <sup> Beginner
docs.text:
<p>H<sub>2</sub>O · E = mc<sup>2</sup> · 1<sup>st</sup> place</p>

H2O · E = mc2 · 1st place

docs.title: <code>, <kbd>, <samp>, <var> Beginner
docs.text:
<p>Call <code>array.map()</code> to transform items.</p>
<p>Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>S</kbd> to save.</p>
<p>The terminal printed <samp>Build succeeded</samp>.</p>
<p>The area is <var>width</var> × <var>height</var>.</p>

Call array.map() to transform items.

Press Ctrl + S to save.

The terminal printed Build succeeded.

The area is width × height.

Tag Meaning code A fragment of computer code kbd Keyboard (or voice) input the user types samp Sample output from a program var A variable in maths or programming

docs.title: <abbr> Abbreviation Beginner
docs.text:
<p>Use <abbr title="Cascading Style Sheets">CSS</abbr> for styling.</p>

Use CSS for styling.

Senior note · 🟠 Advanced

title tooltips aren't available to touch or keyboard users. Spell the abbreviation out the first time it appears in the text, and use <abbr> after that.

docs.title: <cite>, <q>, <dfn> Intermediate
docs.text:
<p>My favourite book is <cite>The Pragmatic Programmer</cite>.</p>
